title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: # 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作 > **内容边界**：下方“授权原文”是官方主内容的 Markdown 转换；中文操作路线、练习与验收由整理者编写，不是作者逐句翻译，也不代表已在本机运行软件验证。 ## 中文任务导读 通过官方行走示例理解关键帧、保持帧、洋葱皮和循环节奏，再迁移到像素角色。 **前提**：能够新建、保存和打开 Krita 文档；先确定目标像素尺寸、色板与透明度要求。 ### 操作路线 1. 进入动画工作区，先设置画布、时间范围和帧率；把背景与动画图层分开。 2. 在动画图层创建关键帧，建立身体与四肢的主要姿势。 3. 开启洋葱皮，用相邻帧对齐头部与脚底，继续补中间姿势。 4. 循环播放并调整帧间距，最后导出图像序列供引擎使用。 ### 配图怎么读 ![从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作：官方示意图](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/animation_walkcycle_2021_4_frames.gif) 循环示例用少量姿势构成连续步态；看脚的接触顺序、身体上下运动以及最后一帧回到第一帧的衔接。 图内界面与作品保留原貌；示例转用于像素素材时仍按本篇验收条件检查。 ### 练习与验收（整理者补充） 制作一个 4～6 个绘制帧的行走循环；固定脚底基线，并分别观察轮廓和最终配色版本。 - [ ] 首尾衔接不突然跳位。 - [ ] 背景层不会随角色帧一起变化。 - [ ] 脚底锚点和帧尺寸一致。 ### 版本与适用边界 官方案例为侧面普通绘画，不是俯视像素成品；姿势与时间轴方法可迁移，视角与像素轮廓需另作设计。 抓取时页面标题标注 **Krita Manual 5.3.0**；这是文档快照版本，不构成已发布软件版本或本机功能的验证。原文中保留的 `Added/Changed/Deprecated in version` 是兼容性依据。 ## 来源、许可与修改记录 - 原文：[Animation with Krita](https://docs.krita.org/en/user_manual/animation.html) - 作者：Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier；Raghavendra Kamath；Scott Petrovic；Lundin - 页内作者与许可原始声明：[RST 源文件](../../sources/asset-production/MAKE-012/original.rst)；[线上原始声明](https://docs.krita.org/en/_sources/user_manual/animation.rst.txt)。 - 许可：[GNU Free Documentation License 1.3 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html)；[本地许可证全文](../../licenses/krita-GFDL-1.3.txt)。各图若有独立作者或许可，沿用原文紧邻图像的署名，不把作品许可自动泛化为文档许可。 - 修改历史：2026-10-29，Codex 为本教程库新增中文导读、练习和验收；将官方 HTML 主内容转换为 Markdown，去除导航与页脚，将控制图标转为文字、将教学图像存为本地文件。正文、步骤、代码、表格与图像说明保留。 - 本修改版沿用 GFDL 1.3 或更新版本。保留作者声明和上游链接；未添加 Invariant Sections、Front-Cover Texts 或 Back-Cover Texts。外链视频、安装包和关联页面没有自动下载或转录。 ## 授权原文（英语，完整主内容转换） ## Animation with Krita Thanks to the 2015 Kickstarter, **Krita** has animation. In specific, **Krita** has frame-by-frame raster animation. To access the animation features, the easiest way is to change your workspace to Animation. This will make the animation dockers and workflow appear. ### Workflow

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Workflow
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: In traditional animation workflow, what you do is that you make [Keyframes](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/animation_timeline.html#term-Keyframe), which contain the important poses, and then draw frames in between (*tweening* in highly sophisticated animator’s jargon). For this workflow, there are three important dockers: 1. The [Animation Timeline Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/animation_timeline.html#timeline-docker). View and control all the frames in your animation. The timeline docker also contains functions to manage your layers. The layers that are created in the timeline docker also appear on the normal Layer docker. 2. The [Onion Skin Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/onion_skin.html#onion-skin-docker). This docker controls the look of the onion skin, which in turn is useful for seeing the previous frame. 3. The [Animation Curves Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/animation_curves.html#animation-curves-docker). This docker allows you to do minor tweening for animation curves. 4. The [Storyboard Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/storyboard_docker.html#storyboard-docker). This docker helps you create and keep track of storyboards. Furthermore, especially when you want to do a big animation, that is, any animation longer than 3 seconds, you will need to think about how you are going to approach this. Krita is specialized in *frame by frame animation*, and because of this Krita keeps all the frames in memory. This means that animation files will eat up all of your computer’s working memory (RAM). If you don’t know what working memory is, you probably have too little to do a long sequence in Krita. Therefore, you need to take a page from professional animation and do some planning! ![Figure 1: The storyboard docker can help you plan out the shots of a scene. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Storyboard_thumbnailonly_view.png) The storyboard docker can help you plan out the shots of a scene.

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Workflow
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text:
Typically, most animation projects start with a script or at the very least an outline of actions that will happen. You can do this in any kind of text editor you like. The next step is to create a [storyboard](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/storyboard_docker.html#storyboard-docker). They are sketches of the basic composition of each scene, with some extra notes on what is going to move, like camera movement, character movement, notes on audio, notes on color. These seem closer to a comic than an animation, but the key difference between the two is that in comics the composition is made to help the reader move their eyes over the page, while in animation the viewer’s eyes will stay in relatively the same spot, so consecutive storyboard frames will have their most important elements in relatively the same place. If that seems a little abstract, don’t worry. You can make a story board by using the animation functions, but the key here is that you use as little frames as possible. Export the story board using the render animation option.

Then, the next step is to make an *Animatic*. An animatic is basically the storyboard, but then animated. You are best off doing this in a video editor like [Kdenlive](http://kdenlive.org/), [OpenShot](https://www.openshot.org/), [Olive](https://olivevideoeditor.org/index.php), or even Windows Movie Maker. *If you want to put everything together into one big animation you will need to learn how to use such a program to begin with, as Krita doesn’t have extensive video and audio montage functions.*

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Workflow
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text:
Doing the animatic will allow you to see how the animation can be subdivided into small clips. If you are just starting out, you are best off limiting yourself to 12 frames per second. Then, a 10-second clip would be 120 frames. Try to figure out if you can subdivide your animation idea into clips of 10 seconds or shorter. You can import the story board frames associated with a specific clip by going to File ‣ Import Animation Frames. From there, slowly start building up your animation. During the sketching phase it may also help to work on a low resolution, like 800×450 pixels. High resolution only starts mattering when you are doing line art, after all. And it will be hard to get to that point if you don’t even have a rough outline.

Always keep an eye on the memory consumption. You can see the memory consumption in the status bar, by clicking the resolution label. This label should also have a little progress bar that shows how much memory Krita is using at this moment. Don’t let the memory bar get full: it will lead to Krita slowing down, and sometimes it might even mean Krita won’t be able to export the animation on your specific machine. You can reduce memory consumption by:

1. Merging together layers. Yes, you cannot afford to have a layer for every single change. Often, the fewer layers, the better.
2. In some cases by going to Image ‣ Crop Layers to Image Size, this will crop all layers to remove sections that are outside the canvas.
3. Sometimes, certain layers don’t need to be full color, especially if they’re just black and white. You can then go to Layers ‣ Convert ‣ Convert Layer Color Space and convert the layer to a grayscale one. This will half the amount of RAM this specific layer will take up.
4. Working smaller. Even if you imagined yourself animating in the 4K resolution, you might need to accept your computer just cannot handle this. Try going a step lower, on animations, even a 20% reduction can make a huge difference in memory consumption, while not being a huge difference in resolution.

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Workflow
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: Also watch out that other programs on your computer aren’t hogging all the RAM. Web browsers and chat programs tend to be the biggest culprits here, especially if you are streaming music or videos. If you are hurting for memory, see if you can get these functions to work on a separate device like a phone instead. Another thing you will want to do is make a ton of backups. Every time you hit an important section with an animation, like you finished the line art, or you did a pretty tricky section, you will want to use File ‣ Incremental Backup to make a separate copy of the current file to continue working in. This way, if the animation file gets corrupt, which could happen due to a power outage, or a cat jumping on the keyboard, you will still have a snapshot of the last important section. Other backup techniques, like copying the files to a cloud service, or to a backup hard drive are also very recommended. Tip And while we’re at it, whenever you’ve hit a milestone, don’t forget to take a break as well! Doing big projects like animations take a lot of effort and concentration, so taking breaks is important to recharge yourself. When you are done, you will want to use Render Animation again. Now either export a frame sequence or a small video file, and then compose all the frame sequences and video files together in the video editor. Then you can render it to `WebM`, and upload it to your favorite video hosting website. This may all seem a little complicated, but if your computer doesn’t have a lot of resources, you have got to be resourceful yourself! ### Introduction to animation: How to make a walk cycle The best way to get to understand all these different parts is to actually use them. Walk cycles are considered the most basic form of a full animation, because of all the different parts involved with them. Therefore, going over how one makes a walk cycle should serve as a good introduction. #### Setup

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Setup
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: First, we make a new file. On the first tab, we type in a nice ratio like 1280×1024, set the dpi to 72 (we’re making this for screens after all) and title the document ‘walk cycle’. In the second tab, we choose a nice background color, and set the background to canvas-color. This means that Krita will automatically fill in any transparent bits with the background color. You can change this in Image ‣ Image Properties. This is very useful for animation, as the layer you do animation on **must** be semi-transparent to get *onion skinning* working. Note Krita has a bunch of functionality for meta-data, starting at the Create Document screen. The title will be automatically used as a suggestion for saving and the description can be used by databases, or for you to leave comments behind. Not many people use it individually, but it can be useful for working in larger groups. Then hit Create! Then, to get all the necessary tools for animation, select the animation workspace in Window ‣ Workspace ‣ Animation Which should result in this: ![Figure 2: The animation workspace adds the Animation Timeline Docker at the bottom. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_01.png) The animation workspace adds the [Animation Timeline Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/animation_timeline.html#timeline-docker) at the bottom. #### Animating Make sure there’s two transparent layers setup in the layer docker. You can add a new layer by pressing the + or by pressing `ins`. Let’s name the bottom one ‘environment’ and the top `walkcycle` by double-clicking their names in the layer docker. ![Figure 3: Layout of the layer stack.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_02.png) Use the [Straight Line Tool](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/tools/line.html#line-tool) to draw a single horizontal line. This is the ground. ![Figure 4: Our simple environment, consisting of a single horizon.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_03.png) Then, select the `walkcycle` layer and draw a head and torso (you can use any brush for this).

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Animating
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text:
![Figure 5: A head and torso.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_04.png)

Now, selecting a new frame will not make a new frame automatically. Krita doesn’t actually see the `walkcycle` layer as an animated layer at all!

We can make it an animated layer by adding a frame to the timeline. A frame in the timeline to get a context menu. Select Create Duplicate Frame ( [duplicateframe] ).

Attention

If you select Create Blank Frame, the content of the layer will be dropped and a new blank frame will appear; since you want to preserve the image, you need to use Create Duplicate Frame.

![Figure 6: Location of the onion skin icon.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_05.png)

You can see it has become an animated layer because of the onion skin icon ( [onionon] ) showing up in the timeline docker.

Use the Create Duplicate Frame button to copy the first frame onto the second. Then, use the [Move Tool](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/tools/move.html#move-tool) (switch to it using the `T` shortcut) with the `Shift + ↑` shortcut to move the frame contents up.

We can see the difference by turning on the onion skinning (press the [onionoff] , so it becomes [onionon] ):

![Figure 7: Onion skin is turned on.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_06.png)

![Figure 8: The current frame in black and the silhouette of the previous frame in red.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_07.png)

Now, you should see the previous frame as red.

Warning

Krita sees white as a color, not as transparent, so make sure the animation layer you are working on is transparent in the bits where there’s no drawing. You can fix the situation by use the [Color to Alpha](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/filters/colors.html#filter-color-to-alpha) filter, but prevention is best.

![Figure 9: Current frame is black and silhouette of the future frame is green.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_08.png)

Future frames are drawn in green, and both colors can be configured in the onion skin docker.

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Animating
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: Now, we’re going to draw the two extremes of the walk cycle. These are the pose where both legs are as far apart as possible, and the pose where one leg is full stretched and the other pulled in, ready to take the next step. ![Figure 10: The above image shows our two extremes: legs far apart, and one leg straight while the other is bent, as it’s taking a step. This also shows the power of onion skins, as we can see both extremes at once. Notice also how the legs have been made semi-transparent. This isn’t necessary with a stick figure, but useful in this case when we start copying. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_09.png) The above image shows our two extremes: legs far apart, and one leg straight while the other is bent, as it’s taking a step. This also shows the power of onion skins, as we can see both extremes at once. Notice also how the legs have been made semi-transparent. This isn’t necessary with a stick figure, but useful in this case when we start copying. Let’s copy these two. You can do this by doing [right mouse button] on the frame, and then selecting Copy Keyframes. Then select the new position in the time line, [right mouse button] again, and Paste Keyframes. Now then… 1. Copy frame 0 to frame 2. 2. Copy frame 1 to frame 3. 3. Erase the semi transparent lines to make it obvious which leg is in front of the other. In 0 and 1, we have the closer leg to the right, then bend, and in 2 and 3, we have the further leg to the right and then bend. ![Figure 11: Introduction to animation 10](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_10.png) 4. In the animation settings, set the frame-rate to 4 ![Figure 12: Introduction to animation 11](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_11.png) 5. Select all frames in the timeline docker by dragging-selecting them. ![Figure 13: Introduction to animation 12](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_12.png) 6. Press play in the header. 7. Enjoy your first animation!

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Animating
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: ![Figure 14: animation walkcycle 2021 4 frames](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/animation_walkcycle_2021_4_frames.gif) #### Expanding upon your rough walk cycle ![Figure 15: Introduction to animation 13](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_13.png) You can quickly make some space by the `Alt + drag` shortcut on any frame. This’ll move that frame and all others after it in one go. More efficient for us, however, is to select all frames, [right mouse button] them, and then select Hold frames ‣ Insert Hold Frame, which will insert an empty space or *Hold Frame* in between each *Keyframe*. Make new frames in between each keyframe, and try to interpolate, or inbetween each frame you add. Note A lot has been written about how to inbetween properly, and it’s one of the areas where animators express their own style the clearest. As such, we won’t cover inbetweening itself here. We recommend you do a search for inbetweening tutorials on the internet. We also recommend animation analyses to get an idea of how intricate this subject is. For this particular example, I prefer to start by finding the position of the heel in a frame, then draw the rest of the foot, then the knees, and then the rest of the legs. ![Figure 16: Introduction to animation 14](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_14.png) ![Figure 15: Introduction to animation 13](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_13.png) You’ll find that the more frames you add, the more difficult it becomes to keep track of the animation. There are two things you can do here. The first is to color label frames, you can do [right mouse button] on the keyframes, and select any of the colors on the bottom. ![Figure 17: In this example, the extremes are blue, the first inbetweens green and the less important inbetweens in yellow and orange. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_13b.png) In this example, the extremes are blue, the first inbetweens green and the less important inbetweens in yellow and orange.

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Expanding upon your rough walk cycle
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: Another thing you can do is to adjust the onion skins. You can modify the onion skin by using the [Onion Skin Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/onion_skin.html#onion-skin-docker), where you can change how many frames are visible at once, by toggling them on the top row. The bottom row is for controlling transparency, while below there you can modify the colors and intensity of the coloring. ![Figure 18: Introduction to animation 15](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_15.png) ![Figure 19: Here we’ve turned off all onion skinned frames except the next and previous ones. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_14b.png) Here we’ve turned off all onion skinned frames except the next and previous ones. #### Animating with multiple layers Okay, our walk cycle is missing some hands, let’s add them on a separate layer. So we make a new layer, and name it hands and… ![Figure 20: Introduction to animation 16](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_16.png) Our walk cycle is gone from the timeline docker! This is a feature actually. A full animation can have so many little parts that an animator might want to remove the layers they’re not working on from the timeline docker. Added in version 4.3.0: In **Krita 4.3.0** and later, all new layers are pinned to the timeline by default. To show a layer whether it’s active or not, you can “pin” it to the timeline by clicking the [pintimeline] icon while having the layer you want pinned selected in the [layer docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/layers.html#layer-docker). We recommend pinning any layers that you’re currently animating on. ![Figure 21: Introduction to animation 17](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_17.png) ![Figure 22: Introduction to animation 18](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_18.png) #### Exporting

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Exporting
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: When you are done, select File ‣ Render Animation. To render to a video file, you’ll need a program called **FFmpeg**. To learn more, please read [Render Animation](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/render_animation.html#render-animation). Enjoy your walk cycle! ![Figure 23: Introduction to animation walkcycle 02](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_walkcycle_02.gif) #### Animating with transform masks Added in version 5.0. If you want to move your walk cycle, you may use [Transform Masks](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/layers_and_masks/transformation_masks.html#transformation-masks) to move the frames from left to right without editing the pixels themselves. First, open up the [Animation Curves Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/animation_curves.html#animation-curves-docker) if it has not been opened yet, under Settings ‣ Dockers ‣ Animation Curves. Then, group the layers that you want to transform, in our example, these are the `hands` and the `walkcycle` layers. [right mouse button] the group, Add ‣ Transform mask. Then, go into the animation docker, select the first frame, and select Adds keyframe to control scalar property ( [scalaradd] ). In the Timeline Docker, *Scalar Frames* will be marked with a diamond. Now select the [Transform Tool](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/tools/transform.html#transform-tool), press the screen and move the group to the start point. Press `Enter` to confirm. Select the last frame in the docker, and then press the screen again, now move everything to the end point. Press Zoom view to fit channel range to view the whole frame. Now, when you press play, you will see the layer contents move. However, it is probably moving too fast. There are two things to reduce that problem: The first is to copy and paste the walk cycle frames, so it repeats 3-4 times, then move the scalar frame to the last frame.

title: 从关键姿势到循环：Krita 行走动画实作
heading: Animating with transform masks
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Raghavendra Kamath
Scott Petrovic
Lundin
text: ![Figure 24: Introduction to animation 19](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_19.png) ![Figure 25: introduction to animation walkcycle 03 simple tween](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/introduction_to_animation_walkcycle_03_simple_tween.gif) This still doesn’t sync the walk cycle directly to the speed it’s moving at. The best method, if a little laborious, is to go to the first frame where one of the feet touches the ground, and then mark that section (for example, using [guides](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/grids_and_guides.html#grids-and-guides-docker)), then, in subsequent frames, use the Transform Tool on each frame to move it so that the foot stays in the same place as long as it’s touching the ground. Do the same for the next bit where a foot touches the ground, and the next, and so on. ![Figure 26: Each place where a foot touches the ground is marked using vertical guides, which allows us to adjust each frame, so the foot stays in place. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_20a.png) Each place where a foot touches the ground is marked using vertical guides, which allows us to adjust each frame, so the foot stays in place. ![Figure 27: Introduction to animation 20b](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_20b.png) ![Figure 28: The animation curve docker after adjusting each frame to be in the right spot. Krita can do curve interpolation (so you can create an ease-in and ease-out type curves), but for a situation like this, per-frame adjustment is quicker. ¶](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/Introduction_to_animation_20c.png) The animation curve docker after adjusting each frame to be in the right spot. Krita can do curve interpolation (so you can create an ease-in and ease-out type curves), but for a situation like this, per-frame adjustment is quicker. After having done all that, you will end up with a smoothly moving walk cycle: ![Figure 29: introduction to animation walkcycle 03 adjusted tween](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-012/introduction_to_animation_walkcycle_03_adjusted_tween.gif)

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier

text: # 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围 > **内容边界**：下方“授权原文”是官方主内容的 Markdown 转换；中文操作路线、练习与验收由整理者编写，不是作者逐句翻译，也不代表已在本机运行软件验证。 ## 中文任务导读 让动画速度由时间安排控制，而不是随意复制帧；理解时间轴上的不同帧状态。 **前提**：能够新建、保存和打开 Krita 文档；先确定目标像素尺寸、色板与透明度要求。 ### 操作路线 1. 把需要编辑的图层固定显示到 Animation Timeline，确认当前帧与当前图层。 2. 先区分创建空白关键帧、复制关键帧和已有内容持续显示的保持区间。 3. 移动或插入关键帧调整动作节奏，必要时用帧颜色帮助区分动作阶段。 4. 设置播放范围和帧率，循环检查后再导出。 ### 配图怎么读 ![动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围：官方示意图](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-013/Animation_Timeline_Docker.png) 带标注的时间轴截图把图层、帧和播放控制放在同一面板；区分当前帧指示与真正存有图像内容的关键帧。 图内界面与作品保留原貌；示例转用于像素素材时仍按本篇验收条件检查。 ### 练习与验收（整理者补充） 为同一待机动作做均匀节奏与“停留后快速摆动”两个版本，保持绘制帧数相同。 - [ ] 没有意外在错误图层上创建帧。 - [ ] 动作时长和帧率可由记录复现。 - [ ] 循环范围不会包含空白尾帧。 ### 版本与适用边界 时间轴教程跨多个 Krita 版本；菜单名、帧状态图示以所用版本为准，先用小文档验证。 抓取时页面标题标注 **Krita Manual 5.3.0**；这是文档快照版本，不构成已发布软件版本或本机功能的验证。原文中保留的 `Added/Changed/Deprecated in version` 是兼容性依据。 ## 来源、许可与修改记录 - 原文：[Animation Timeline Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/animation_timeline.html) - 作者：Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier；Dmitry Kazakov；Emmet O'Neill - 页内作者与许可原始声明：[RST 源文件](../../sources/asset-production/MAKE-013/original.rst)；[线上原始声明](https://docs.krita.org/en/_sources/reference_manual/dockers/animation_timeline.rst.txt)。 - 许可：[GNU Free Documentation License 1.3 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html)；[本地许可证全文](../../licenses/krita-GFDL-1.3.txt)。各图若有独立作者或许可，沿用原文紧邻图像的署名，不把作品许可自动泛化为文档许可。 - 修改历史：2026-10-29，Codex 为本教程库新增中文导读、练习和验收；将官方 HTML 主内容转换为 Markdown，去除导航与页脚，将控制图标转为文字、将教学图像存为本地文件。正文、步骤、代码、表格与图像说明保留。 - 本修改版沿用 GFDL 1.3 或更新版本。保留作者声明和上游链接；未添加 Invariant Sections、Front-Cover Texts 或 Back-Cover Texts。外链视频、安装包和关联页面没有自动下载或转录。 ## 授权原文（英语，完整主内容转换） ## Animation Timeline Docker The *Animation Timeline Docker* is at the heart of **Krita**’s raster animation tools, providing everything you need to create, edit and preview traditional hand-drawn animations. ![Figure 1: Animation Timeline Docker](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-013/Animation_Timeline_Docker.png) ### Overview

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Overview
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text:
As shown in the image above, Krita’s Animation Timeline Docker can be thought of as different sections:

1. *Utilities* – The left side of the toolbar gives animators quick access to all of the widgets that are critical to their workflow; *transport controls* (previous, play/pause, stop and next buttons), a frame counter, preview controls (speed and drop frames), and buttons for quickly creating new frames and deleting unwanted ones.
2. *Settings* – While all of the high-traffic controls are presented directly, the right end of the toolbar also contains buttons for opening submenus for things like [Onion Skin Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/onion_skin.html#onion-skin-docker) and settings that you can generally set and forget (for example: playback range, frame rate and autokey mode).
3. *Layer List* – This area contains some subset of the layers of your current document. Similar to the [Layers](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/layers.html#layer-docker), each layer has various properties that can also be toggled here (visibility, locking, onion skins, etc.). While the currently active layer is always shown here, layers can also be “pinned” to the timeline using the pin button to the left of each layer’s name, the Pin to Timeline menu action, or the Pin Existing Layer submenu so they will be visible even when inactive.

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Overview
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text: > > Tip > > > > Depending on your preference, newly created paint layers can start pinned or unpinned by setting the Automatically pin new layers to timeline option in Settings –> Configure Krita… –> General –> Miscellaneous. > > > > Active Layer: > : The *active layer* is the layer that you’re currently able to edit or draw on, shown as a highlighted row in the layer list. [left mouse button] a layer within the layer list will make it the currently active layer. > > > Layer Menu: > : A small menu for manipulating *animated layers* at the top left of the layer list. You can create new layers, remove existing ones, as well as pin or unpin the active layer. (This menu also shows up when [right mouse button] on layer headers inside of the Layer List.) > > > Audio Menu: > : Another small menu at the top of the layer list for animating along with audio sources. This is also where you can open or close audio sources and control output volume/muting. > > > Zoom Handle: > : This special widget allows you to zoom in and out on the frame table, centered around the current frame time. [left mouse button] `+ drag` from within the zoom handle controls the zoom level. 4. *Frame Table* – The *frame table* is a large grid of cells which can either hold a single keyframe or be empty. Each row of the frame table represents an *animated layer* and each column represents a *frame time*. Just like the layer list, the active layer is highlighted across the entire frame table. For those who are familiar with pen-and-paper animation, you can think of the frame table as Krita’s *dope sheet* or time sheet.

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Overview
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text: > > Note > > > > It’s important to understand that frame timings are not based on units of time like seconds, but on *frames*, which can then be played back at any speed, depending on the animation’s *frame rate* and *play speed* settings. > > Keyframes can be moved around the timeline by [left mouse button] `+ drag` shortcut from one slot to another, even across layers. Furthermore, holding the `Ctrl` key while dragging creates a copy, and holding the `Alt` key while dragging creates a clone frame. Finally, [right mouse button] anywhere in the frame table will bring up a context menu for adding, removing, copying, pasting or adjusting timing. > > > > Active Keyframe > : Right now, it’s only possible to view and draw on one keyframe at a time. This is known as the *active keyframe*, and is represented on the frame table as a block filled with diagonal stripes. Often, in simple animations, the active keyframe will be the frame on the active layer that is on or just before the current time. However, if the active keyframe has one or more [clone frames](#term-Clone-frames) all drawing, painting and editing will also affect all of its clones. > > > Clone frames > : A *clone frame* of a keyframe is a reference to that keyframe at a different position. Clone frames share the exact same image data under the hood, and will have the same diagonal markings as the active frame when an active frame with clone frames is selected. > > > Duplicate keyframe > : Not to be confused with [Clone Frames](#term-Clone-frames), a duplicate frame is merely the [Active Keyframe](#term-Active-Keyframe) copied and pasted as a separate [Keyframe](#term-Keyframe). Where clone frames will automatically duplicate the changes you make to them to each cloned frame, a duplicated frame is just another keyframe that happens to have the same content as the source. > > > Current Selection > : Frames highlighted in orange represent a selection or multiple selections. While multiple frames are selected, [right mouse button] anywhere in the frame table will bring up a context menu that will allow for adding and removing keyframes or holds within the current selection. It’s also possible to have multiple separate (non-contiguous) selections if needed. > > > Warning > > > > Painting always happens *only* on the [active keyframe](#term-Active-Keyframe), which is not necessarily part of your current selection on the timeline! > > > Keyframe > : In **Krita**, we call the images that make up your animation *keyframes*. Each keyframe can also be assigned a [Color Label](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/layers.html#term-Color-Label), as a matter of personal organization and workflow. > > > Blank Keyframe > : Within the frame table, keyframes that contain drawings are displayed as *filled blocks* within a cell, while a *blank keyframe* is shown as a *hollow outline*. Unlike some other tools, **Krita** automatically holds each keyframe until the next keyframe on that layer; these *holds* are shown as a *colored line* that’s drawn across all held frames. > > > Frame Timing Header > : The frame timing header is a ruler at the top of the frame table. This header is divided into small notched sections which are based on the current *frame rate* (set in the animation settings submenu at the right end of the toolbar). While each frame is marked with a single line, each second is marked by a subtle double-line. Major notches are also marked by a frame number. > > > Cached Frames > : The frame timing header also shows important information about which frames are currently *cached*. When something is said to be “cached”, that means that it is stored in your device’s working memory (RAM) for extra fast access. Cached frames are shown by the header with a small light-gray rectangle in each column. While this information isn’t always critical for us artists, it’s helpful to know that Krita is working behind the curtains to cache our animation frames for the smoothest possible experience when scrubbing through or playing back your animation. > > > Current Time Scrubber: > : A highlighted column in the frame table which controls the current frame time and, as such, what is currently displayed in the viewport. > > > Zoomable Scrollbar > : Not only can the scrollbars on the Animation Timeline Docker be used to *pan* the frame table by dragging left and right, it can also be used to quickly *zoom* in and out by dragging up and down. Pan and zoom in one flick of a wrist! 5. *Onion Skins Docker* – While technically a separate docker, the [Onion Skin Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/onion_skin.html#onion-skin-docker) is used in conjunction with the Animation Timeline docker to help animators see how their animation changes between neighboring keyframes. The onion skins menu button on the Animation Timeline Docker can be used to quickly toggle the visibility of the Onion Skins Docker.

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Overview
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text: ### Animating In order to begin animating with **Krita**, we first need to turn our paint layer into an *animated layer* by adding our first [keyframe](#term-Keyframe). In our case we will start with a [blank keyframe](#term-Blank-Keyframe), but if you’ve already drawn something on the paint layer and would like to transfer it to your new keyframe you can create a [duplicate keyframe](#term-Duplicate-keyframe) instead. To make a new, blank keyframe, [right mouse button] any square on the timeline docker and select Create Blank Frame. A blank frame (one that you haven’t yet drawn anything in) appears as a *hollow outline* instead of a solid box, making that frame active and drawing on the canvas will make it appear as a *solid, colored rectangle*. To move a keyframe around, you can drag and drop it into another empty frame slot, even across animation layers. The currently selected layer will automatically be shown on the timeline. However, while animating you may find that you want to keep another layer “pinned”, making it visible in the Animation Timeline Docker regardless of which layer is selected. There are a few ways to do this in Krita, but it doesn’t get any simpler than [left mouse button] on the little pushpin icon next to the layer’s name. It’s not much of an animation with only one frame, so to add another new frame you can do the same thing we did last time by selecting Create Blank Frame from the [right mouse button] menu or by double- [left mouse button] on a particular frame slot. For the sake of this lesson, however, we will mix it up by creating a duplicate keyframe by scrubbing to a different *time* and press the Create Duplicate Keyframe button on toolbar at the top of the Animation Timeline Docker. As you can see, there are quick a few convenient ways to add or remove keyframes from your animation in Krita, depending on your personal preference, input devices and workflow!

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Animating
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text: Now that we have more than one keyframe, we can do different drawings in each and play back our simple animation by press the Play/Pause button on the toolbar at the top of the docker. Another crucial technique for animating is manually switching between frames at your own pace to inspect the frame-by-frame movement of your animation as you work, also known as “scrubbing”. Like everything else, we’ve made sure that there are a few different ways to scrub through you animation, but one of my favorites is to simply [left mouse button] `+ drag` between different times on the [Frame Timing Header](#term-Frame-Timing-Header) at the top of the frame table. I know that’s a lot of info to digest, but all you really need to know to get started is how to create new keyframes and scrub through your animation to check your progress. From there, all that’s left is the hard but rewarding work of drawing lots and lots (and lots) of animation frames! ### Tips

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Tips
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text:
- There are a couple subtle features built into the docker’s transport controls that you might find useful. For example, press the Stop button *while your animation is playing* will jump back to whatever frame you started playing from, and press it again *when your animation is not playing* will jump back to the first frame of your animation. Similarly, the next keyframe button will jump the selection to the next available keyframe on the active layer, but *if there is no next keyframe on that layer it will use the timing of your animation to estimate where you may want to place your next keyframe, and jump to that position.* While a bit advanced, nuances like this mean that the Animation Timeline Docker’s buttons (and keybind-able actions) almost always do something useful for animators.
- It’s possible to add multiple keyframes by [right mouse button] inside the frame table and selecting the Keyframes ‣ Insert Multiple Keyframes pop-up submenu item. With this option you can specify the number of frames to add with the option of built in timing for quickly creating a series of 1s, 2s, 3s, etc. These settings are saved between uses.
- You can also change the color of keyframes within the frame table so that you can easily identify important frames or distinguish between different sections of your animation. The current color selection is remembered for new frames so that you can easily make a set of colored frames and then switch to another color. (By the way, it’s even possible to quickly jump between frames of the same color by assigning a keyboard shortcut to Previous/Next Matching Keyframe.)
- [right mouse button] within the [Frame Timing Header](#term-Frame-Timing-Header) instead of the frame table gives you access to a few more option which allow you to add or remove entire columns of frames or holds at a time, as well as reset your animation cache if needed. For example, selecting the Keyframe Columns ‣ Insert Keyframe Column Left pop-up submenu item will add new frames to each layer that’s currently visible in the Timeline Docker.

![Figure 2: Timeline insertkeys](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-013/Timeline_insertkeys.png)

title: 动画时间轴：关键帧、保持帧与播放范围
heading: Tips
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Dmitry Kazakov
Emmet O'Neill
text: - To delete frames, [right mouse button] the frame and press Remove Keyframe. This will delete all selected frames. Similarly, selecting Remove Frame and Pull will delete the selected frames and pull or shift all subsequent frames back/left as much as possible. ### Controls 1. *Layer List* > - [left mouse button] : Select active layer. > - [right mouse button] : Layers Menu (add/remove/show layers, etc.). 2. [Frame Timing Header](#term-Frame-Timing-Header) > - [left mouse button] : Move to time and select frame of the active layer. > - [left mouse button] `+ drag` : Scrub through time and select frame of the active layer. > - [right mouse button] : Frame Columns Menu (insert/remove/copy/paste columns and hold columns). 3. *Frames Table* > - [left mouse button] : Selects a single frame or slot and switches time, but *does not switch active layer*. > - `Space +` [left mouse button] : Pan. > - `Space +` [right mouse button] : Zoom. 4. *Frames Table* (On Empty Slot). > - [right mouse button] : Frames menu (insert/copy/paste frames and insert/remove holds). > - [left mouse button] `+ drag` : Select multiple frames and switch time to the last selected, but *does not switch active layer*. > - `Shift +` [left mouse button] : Select all frames between the active and the clicked frame. > - `Ctrl +` [left mouse button] : Select individual frames together. [left mouse button] `+ drag` them into place. 5. *Frames Table* (On Existing Frame) > - [right mouse button] : Frames menu (remove/copy/paste frames and insert/remove holds). > - [left mouse button] `+ drag` : *Move* a frame or multiple frames. > - `Ctrl +` [left mouse button] `+ drag` : Copy a frame or multiple frames. > - `Alt +` [left mouse button] `+ drag` : Clone a frame or multiple frames. > - `Shift +` [left mouse button] `+ drag` : Move selected frame(s) and *all* the frames to the right of it. (This is useful for when you need to clear up some space in your animation, but don’t want to select all the frames to the right of a particular frame!) ## 本地配图清单

heading: 洋葱皮：比较前后姿势与消除帧间漂移
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
text: # 洋葱皮：比较前后姿势与消除帧间漂移 > **内容边界**：下方“授权原文”是官方主内容的 Markdown 转换；中文操作路线、练习与验收由整理者编写，不是作者逐句翻译，也不代表已在本机运行软件验证。 ## 中文任务导读 在当前帧上显示前后关键姿势，检查轮廓变化、重心和锚点。 **前提**：能够新建、保存和打开 Krita 文档；先确定目标像素尺寸、色板与透明度要求。 ### 操作路线 1. 在包含关键帧的透明动画图层上打开灯泡图标。 2. 在 Onion Skin Docker 选定要显示的前后帧偏移，先只保留最近一帧。 3. 调节总透明度、每个偏移的透明度与前后帧颜色，保持当前帧最清楚。 4. 逐帧检查脚底、头部及道具位置，修正无意的漂移，再关闭洋葱皮看真实播放。 ### 配图怎么读 ![洋葱皮：比较前后姿势与消除帧间漂移：官方示意图](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-014/Onion_skin_docker.png) 洋葱皮面板把当前帧两侧的偏移分开控制，红绿颜色区分过去与未来；透明度只影响参照，不应写进输出图。 图内界面与作品保留原貌；示例转用于像素素材时仍按本篇验收条件检查。 ### 练习与验收（整理者补充） 用洋葱皮检查一个四帧眨眼或呼吸循环，列出并修正三处无意移动。 - [ ] 当前帧与参考帧可清晰区分。 - [ ] 背景的白色没有被误当透明。 - [ ] 关闭洋葱皮后最终轮廓无残留。 ### 版本与适用边界 完全不透明的默认像素图层不能正常提供所需洋葱皮效果；使用新建透明动画图层。 抓取时页面标题标注 **Krita Manual 5.3.0**；这是文档快照版本，不构成已发布软件版本或本机功能的验证。原文中保留的 `Added/Changed/Deprecated in version` 是兼容性依据。 ## 来源、许可与修改记录 - 原文：[Onion Skin Docker](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/dockers/onion_skin.html) - 作者：Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier - 页内作者与许可原始声明：[RST 源文件](../../sources/asset-production/MAKE-014/original.rst)；[线上原始声明](https://docs.krita.org/en/_sources/reference_manual/dockers/onion_skin.rst.txt)。 - 许可：[GNU Free Documentation License 1.3 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html)；[本地许可证全文](../../licenses/krita-GFDL-1.3.txt)。各图若有独立作者或许可，沿用原文紧邻图像的署名，不把作品许可自动泛化为文档许可。 - 修改历史：2026-10-29，Codex 为本教程库新增中文导读、练习和验收；将官方 HTML 主内容转换为 Markdown，去除导航与页脚，将控制图标转为文字、将教学图像存为本地文件。正文、步骤、代码、表格与图像说明保留。 - 本修改版沿用 GFDL 1.3 或更新版本。保留作者声明和上游链接；未添加 Invariant Sections、Front-Cover Texts 或 Back-Cover Texts。外链视频、安装包和关联页面没有自动下载或转录。 ## 授权原文（英语，完整主内容转换） ## Onion Skin Docker ![Figure 1: Onion skin docker](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-014/Onion_skin_docker.png) To make animation easier, it helps to see both the next frame as well as the previous frame sort of layered on top of the current. This is called *onion-skinning*. ![Figure 2: Onion skin 01](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-014/Onion_skin_01.png) Basically, they are images that represent the frames before and after the current frame, usually colored or tinted.

title: 洋葱皮：比较前后姿势与消除帧间漂移
heading: Onion Skin Docker
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
text:
You can toggle them by clicking the lightbulb icon on a layer that is animated (so, has frames), and isn’t fully opaque. (Krita will consider white to be white, not transparent, so don’t animated on an opaque layer if you want onion skins.)

Changed in version 4.2: Since 4.2 onion skins are disabled on layers whose default pixel is fully opaque. These layers can currently only be created by using background as raster layer in the content section of the new image dialog. Just don’t try to animate on a layer like this if you rely on onion skins, instead make a new one.

The term onionskin comes from the fact that onions are semi-transparent. In traditional animation animators would make their initial animations on semitransparent paper on top of an light-table (of the special animators variety), and they’d start with so called keyframes, and then draw frames in between. For that, they would place said keyframes below the frame they were working on, and the light table would make the lines of the keyframes shine through, so they could reference them.

Onion-skinning is a digital implementation of such a workflow, and it’s very useful when trying to animate.

![Figure 3: Onion skin 02](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-014/Onion_skin_02.png)

The slider and the button with zero offset control the master opacity and visibility of all the onion skins. The boxes at the top allow you to toggle them on and off quickly, the main slider in the middle is a sort of ‘master transparency’ while the sliders to the side allow you to control the transparency per keyframe offset.

Tint controls how strongly the frames are tinted, the first screen has 100%, which creates a silhouette, while below you can still see a bit of the original colors at 50%.

The Previous Frame and Next Frame color labels allows you set the colors.

title: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
heading: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
author: Scott Petrovic
Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Beelzy
Lewis Fuller Hill
text: # 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码 > **内容边界**：下方“授权原文”是官方主内容的 Markdown 转换；中文操作路线、练习与验收由整理者编写，不是作者逐句翻译，也不代表已在本机运行软件验证。 ## 中文任务导读 把可编辑动画变成引擎可接收的图像序列，同时理解预览视频的缩放与编码限制。 **前提**：能够新建、保存和打开 Krita 文档；先确定目标像素尺寸、色板与透明度要求。 ### 操作路线 1. 设置 First Frame 与 Last Frame，并核对导出范围是否包含完整循环。 2. 启用图像序列导出，选择保存位置、基础名称与编号起点。 3. 区分逐时间帧导出与 Only Unique Frames；后者需要另行保留各关键帧的持续时长。 4. 需要放大预览时选整数倍和 Nearest Neighbour；保存后检查透明度、帧数与顺序。 ### 配图怎么读 ![导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码：官方示意图](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-015/ffmpeg_screenshot_path.png) 导出窗口同时显示序列与视频设置；源截图采用旧版界面，重点识别范围、尺寸和编码器字段，再对照所用版本。 图内界面与作品保留原貌；示例转用于像素素材时仍按本篇验收条件检查。 ### 练习与验收（整理者补充） 把同一循环导出为透明 PNG 序列与两倍预览，比较每帧尺寸和时长是否可重建。 - [ ] 实际序列帧数与导出范围对应。 - [ ] 透明资产没有只保留带黑底的视频。 - [ ] 放大预览没有引入模糊插值。 ### 版本与适用边界 手册注明 5.2 起包含部分 FFmpeg 功能；Android 路径不同。原文某些旧编号例子可能有笔误，实际文件名需检查。 抓取时页面标题标注 **Krita Manual 5.3.0**；这是文档快照版本，不构成已发布软件版本或本机功能的验证。原文中保留的 `Added/Changed/Deprecated in version` 是兼容性依据。 ## 来源、许可与修改记录 - 原文：[Render Animation](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/render_animation.html) - 作者：Scott Petrovic；Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier；Beelzy；Lewis Fuller Hill - 页内作者与许可原始声明：[RST 源文件](../../sources/asset-production/MAKE-015/original.rst)；[线上原始声明](https://docs.krita.org/en/_sources/reference_manual/render_animation.rst.txt)。 - 许可：[GNU Free Documentation License 1.3 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html)；[本地许可证全文](../../licenses/krita-GFDL-1.3.txt)。各图若有独立作者或许可，沿用原文紧邻图像的署名，不把作品许可自动泛化为文档许可。 - 修改历史：2026-10-29，Codex 为本教程库新增中文导读、练习和验收；将官方 HTML 主内容转换为 Markdown，去除导航与页脚，将控制图标转为文字、将教学图像存为本地文件。正文、步骤、代码、表格与图像说明保留。 - 本修改版沿用 GFDL 1.3 或更新版本。保留作者声明和上游链接；未添加 Invariant Sections、Front-Cover Texts 或 Back-Cover Texts。外链视频、安装包和关联页面没有自动下载或转录。 ## 授权原文（英语，完整主内容转换） ## Render Animation Render animation allows you to render your animation to an image sequence and to `.gif`, `.mp4`, `.mkv`, or other video files.

title: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
heading: Render Animation
author: Scott Petrovic
Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Beelzy
Lewis Fuller Hill
text: For rendering to an animated file format, Krita will first render to a PNG sequence and then use a video encoder to render that sequence to an animated file format. The reason for this two-step process is that animation files can be really complex and really big, and this is the best way to allow you to keep control over the export process. For example, if your computer has a hiccup, and one frame saves out weird, first saving the image sequence allows you to only resave that one weird frame before rendering. This means that you will need to find a good place to stick your frames before you can start rendering. If you only do throwaway animations, you can use a spot on your hard-drive with enough room and select Delete Sequence After Rendering. Note On Android, file handling and video rendering works differently. You can only either export an image sequence or a video, not both. FFmpeg is not used, do not attempt to install it. ### General First Frame : The first frame of the range of frames you wish to adjust. Automatically set to the first frame of your current selection in the timeline. This is useful when you only want to re-render a little part. Last Frame : As above, the last frame of the range of frames you wish to adjust. Automatically set to the last frame of your current selection in the timeline. ### Export as Image Sequence File Format : The file format to export the sequence to. When rendering we enforce PNG. The usual export options can be modified with the edit button next to the drop-down. Image Location : Where you render the image sequence to. Some people prefer to use a flash-drive or perhaps a harddrive that is fast. On Android, you will be prompted for a directory instead. Base Name : The base name of your image sequence. This will get suffixed with a number depending on the frame.

title: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
heading: Export as Image Sequence
author: Scott Petrovic
Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Beelzy
Lewis Fuller Hill
text: Start numbering at : The frames are named by using Base Name above and adding a number for the frame. This allows you to set where the frame number starts, so rendering from 8 to 10 with starting point 3 will give you images named 11 and 15. Useful for programs that don’t understand sequences starting with 0, or for precision output. Only Unique Frames : Normally Krita generates a frame for every FPS in the sequence. Ticking this will only generate keyframes, saving space. ### Export as Video Width : Set the desired width in pixels. Height : Set the desired height in pixels. FPS : Set the desired frames per second. Note Widths and heights above 1920 pixels and FPS values beyond 30 are not widely supported. They can cause the video export to fail outright or the resulting video may not play back properly on some devices. Krita will warn you about this, but still allows you to try such exports. Some video formats require width and height to be even numbers. Krita will automatically adjust the size if necessary. Filter : Set the scaling filter. Bicubic is fine for most cases, but if you want to, say, export a pixel art animation at twice the size, Nearest Neighbour will preserve the fine details better. Render As : The file format to render to. Some have extra options that can be manipulated via the edit button next to the drop-down. Video Location : Location and name of the rendered animation. On Android, you will be prompted for a file name instead. Include Audio : Include any audio you have added. FFmpeg : The location where your have FFmpeg. On Android, the operating system’s video encoder is used instead. Changed in version 5.2: This is now optional. Krita’s bundled FFMpeg functionality is able to provide some options, but it is still useful to set this if you want to use a specific version of FFMpeg for rendering videos.

title: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
heading: Export as Video
author: Scott Petrovic
Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Beelzy
Lewis Fuller Hill
text: Delete Sequence After Rendering : Delete the prerendered image sequence after done rendering. This allows you to choose whether to try and save some space, or to save the sequence for when encoding fails. On Android, the image sequence is only stored internally and always deleted afterwards. Deprecated since version 5.2: Since 5.2, Krita will always delete the image sequence if Export as Image Sequence is not checked while Export as Video is. Warning Krita currently does not support rendering video with transparent elements, and will instead render them as black. To combat this, you can add in a fully colored, opaque layer at the bottom of the file before rendering. ### Setting Up Krita for Exporting Animations Changed in version 5.2. Since Krita 5.2, Krita bundles a small part of FFmpeg. This means that you will not strictly have to download and setup FFMpeg to render animations. Different versions of the program have different options however, and video experts might want to use a specific version of FFMpeg to get more codec options. The bundled FFmpeg supports the following containers: `Webm`, `Matroska` and `OGG`, which are a wrapper around the video data (amongst others), which are encoded with codecs, of which the bundled FFMpeg supports: - AOM AV1 - VPX VP9 - VPX VP8 - 8. 264 (via openH264) - Theora The following instructions will explain how to get a non-bundled version of FFMpeg and set it up. The setup is a one-time thing so you won’t have to do it again. #### Step 1 - Downloading FFmpeg ##### For Windows Open the FFmpeg [download page.](https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/) Go to release section and choose the download link that says `ffmpeg-release-essentials.zip`. Note **Don’t** download the file which filename contains the word `shared`. It won’t work with Krita.

title: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
heading: For Windows
author: Scott Petrovic
Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Beelzy
Lewis Fuller Hill
text: If the filename ends with `.7z`, you can still use it, but then you need to have a program that can open 7zip archives (for example [7zip itself](https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/)). In case of a `.zip` file, you can open it just using the Windows file browser. ##### For macOS Please see the section above. However, FFmpeg is obtained from [here](https://evermeet.cx/ffmpeg/) instead. Just pick the big green button on the left under the FFmpeg heading. You will also need an archiving utility that supports .7z, since FFmpeg provides their macOS builds in .7z format. If you don’t have one, try something like [Keka](https://www.kekaosx.com). Alternatively you can find the smaller text under the big green button that says Download as ZIP. Then you should be able to extract it just using Finder. ##### For Linux FFmpeg can be installed from the repositories on most Linux systems. Version 2.6 is required for proper GIF support, as we use the palettegen functionality. ##### For Android Krita does not use FFmpeg on Android. Don’t attempt to install it. #### Step 2 - Unzipping and Linking to Krita ##### For Windows Once you’ve downloaded, go to the file location. Right click on the FFmpeg file, and select `Extract All...`. Select the file destination, and rename the file to ‘ffmpeg’. Hint It is easiest to save the file under C: drive, but any location is fine. Open Krita back up and go to File ‣ Render Animation…. Under `Export > Video`, click the file icon next to FFmpeg. Select this file `C:/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe` and click OK. ![Figure 1: FFmpeg path.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-015/ffmpeg_screenshot_path.png) Tip If you have saved FFmpeg to a different location, choose `/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg.exe`. ##### For macOS After downloading FFmpeg, you just need to extract it and then simply point to it in the FFmpeg location in Krita like `/Users/user/Downloads/ffmpeg` (assuming you downloaded and extracted the .7z file to /Users/user/Downloads).

title: 导出动画：PNG 序列、像素放大与编码
heading: For Linux
author: Scott Petrovic
Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
Beelzy
Lewis Fuller Hill
text: ##### For Linux FFmpeg is, if installed from the repositories, usually found in `/usr/bin/ffmpeg`. #### Step 3 - Testing out an animation ffmpeg.exe is what Krita uses to do all of its animation export magic. Now that it is hooked up, let us test it out. Let’s make an animated GIF. In the Render Animation dialog, change the Render As field to “GIF image”. Choose the file location where it will save with the “File” menu below. I just saved it to my desktop and called it “*export.gif*”. When it is done, you should be able to open it up and see the animation. Warning By default, FFmpeg will render MP4 files with a too new codec, which means that Windows Media Player won’t be able to play it. So for Windows, select “baseline” for the profile instead of “high422” before rendering. Note macOS does not come with any software to play MP4 and MKV files. If you use Chrome for your web browser, you can drag the video file into that and the video should play. Otherwise you will need to get a program like VLC to see the video. ## 本地配图清单 | 图 | 本地文件 | 原始来源 | |---|---|---| | 1 | [Figure 1: FFmpeg path.](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-015/ffmpeg_screenshot_path.png) | [原图](https://docs.krita.org/en/_images/ffmpeg_screenshot_path.png) |

title: 导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算
heading: 导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
text: # 导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算 > **内容边界**：下方“授权原文”是官方主内容的 Markdown 转换；中文操作路线、练习与验收由整理者编写，不是作者逐句翻译，也不代表已在本机运行软件验证。 ## 中文任务导读 把已有角色动作导入为可编辑帧，避免文件排序和帧率变化造成动作错乱。 **前提**：能够新建、保存和打开 Krita 文档；先确定目标像素尺寸、色板与透明度要求。 ### 操作路线 1. 精灵表需先按确定的行列或切片数拆成等尺寸图像；原文示例展示九张精灵的切分。 2. 新建目标文档，通过 File → Import Animation Frames 添加图像。 3. 检查数字排序与字母排序，尤其是 frame_2 和 frame_10 等未补零名称。 4. 设置 Start at 与 Step；例如 6 fps 的动作进入 24 fps 文档，可用 Step=4 保持时长。 ### 配图怎么读 ![导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算：官方示意图](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-016/Animation_split_spritesheet.png) 第一张图展示在等间隔精灵表上切分；后续图片展示添加序列与导入后的时间轴，注意切片数和输出帧数的差别。 图内界面与作品保留原貌；示例转用于像素素材时仍按本篇验收条件检查。 ### 练习与验收（整理者补充） 把六张编号帧导入 24 fps 文档，先采用 Step=1 再改为 Step=4，记录时长区别。 - [ ] 帧顺序与动作原意相同。 - [ ] 所有帧画布与锚点一致。 - [ ] 导入后的动作时长与目标一致。 ### 版本与适用边界 原文演示使用 Libre Pixel Cup 角色，引用保留在原文脚注；下载成品用于游戏时需另核资产许可和署名。 抓取时页面标题标注 **Krita Manual 5.3.0**；这是文档快照版本，不构成已发布软件版本或本机功能的验证。原文中保留的 `Added/Changed/Deprecated in version` 是兼容性依据。 ## 来源、许可与修改记录 - 原文：[Import Animation](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/import_animation.html) - 作者：Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier - 页内作者与许可原始声明：[RST 源文件](../../sources/asset-production/MAKE-016/original.rst)；[线上原始声明](https://docs.krita.org/en/_sources/reference_manual/import_animation.rst.txt)。 - 许可：[GNU Free Documentation License 1.3 or later](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/fdl-1.3.html)；[本地许可证全文](../../licenses/krita-GFDL-1.3.txt)。各图若有独立作者或许可，沿用原文紧邻图像的署名，不把作品许可自动泛化为文档许可。 - 修改历史：2026-10-29，Codex 为本教程库新增中文导读、练习和验收；将官方 HTML 主内容转换为 Markdown，去除导航与页脚，将控制图标转为文字、将教学图像存为本地文件。正文、步骤、代码、表格与图像说明保留。 - 本修改版沿用 GFDL 1.3 或更新版本。保留作者声明和上游链接；未添加 Invariant Sections、Front-Cover Texts 或 Back-Cover Texts。外链视频、安装包和关联页面没有自动下载或转录。 ## 授权原文（英语，完整主内容转换） ## Import Animation Krita has several options for allowing you to import an animation. ### Import Frames Frame import will import a list of images into an animation layer. This is a format that most other animation software can export, and thus very useful for interchange. First let us take a sprite sheet from Open Game Art. (This is the Libre Pixel Cup male walkcycle [[1]](#id4)).

title: 导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算
heading: Import Frames
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
text: We’ll use [Image Split](https://docs.krita.org/en/reference_manual/image_split.html#image-split) to split up the sprite sheet. ![Figure 1: Animation split spritesheet](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-016/Animation_split_spritesheet.png) The slices are even, so for a sprite sheet of 9 sprites, use 8 vertical slices and 0 horizontal slices. Give it a proper name and save it as png. Then, make a new canvas, and select File ‣ Import Animation Frames. This will give you a little window. Select Add images. This should get you a file browser where you can select your images. ![Figure 2: Animation import sprites](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-016/Animation_import_sprites.png) You can select multiple images at once. ![Figure 3: Animation set everything](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-016/Animation_set_everything.png) The frames are currently automatically ordered. You can set the ordering with the top-left two drop-down boxes. Press OK, and your animation should be imported as a new layer. ![Figure 4: Animation import done](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-016/Animation_import_done.png) Add images. : Add frames. You can select multiple frames in the file chooser. Remove. : Remove the selected frame Add hold frames automatically. : If a frame sequence has gaps, such as a sequence that has frames 1, 2 and 5, ticking this option will input empty frames at 3 and 4. #### Order Ascending vs Descending : Whether it will import the frames in order from lowest to highest (ascending), or from highest to lowest (descending). Numerical vs Alphabetical : Whether it will use numbers or Alphabetical ordering for the frames. #### Timing Start at : The frame number to import at. Importing at 3 will have the resulting animation start at frame 3 within Krita. Step : The amount of frames to input for each imported frame. For importing a 6 fps animation into a 24 fps animation, you will need to set this to 24 / 6 = 4. This will ensure the playback speed stays the same.

title: 导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算
heading: Timing
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
text: Source FPS : This displays what Krita thinks the fps of the input is with the current timing settings. You can use this to make sure that the input you made is correct with the FPS of your document. ### Import video file Video import allows you to import a sample of a video file as an animated paint layer. Note On Android, importing video files is unavailable. You have to use a computer to import the video, save it to a KRA file and transfer it to your device. ![Figure 5: import video](../../assets/asset-production/MAKE-016/import_video.png) Choose a video file : This will bring up a file chooser for you to select the file in question. Preview : Gives a preview of the file to import. Slider : Allows you to scrub through the file in question. Frame Counter : Allows you to select the frame in question Frame Switcher : Two buttons to switch per frame. #### Video file info Width : The width of the current file. Height : The height of the current file. Duration : The duration in seconds. Frames : The total amount of frames FPS : The frames per second. Color Primaries : The name of the color space primaries Krita has detected. These will be used for the color profile with which the file imports. Only shows up on files where this data is detected. Color Transfer : The name of the color space trc that Krita has found. This too will be used for the color profile. Only shows up on files where this data is detected. #### Import Options FPS : The FPS to import at. Importing 2 seconds of footage at 24 fps will import 48 frames, and at 60 fps, 120 frames will be imported. Skip Interval : Same as Step in the [Import Frames](#import-frames) section. Start at : Time code to start at. Duration : Length of the imported animation. Import into : Document to import the file into. Options are current document and new document. With new document, extra options become available on the second tab. Warning

title: 导入精灵表与序列帧：顺序和帧率换算
heading: Import Options
author: Wolthera van Hövell tot Westerflier
text: Videos, because you usually only play them in a media player, are compressed in special ways. Because Krita is designed to allow you to draw each individual frame, this data gets uncompressed. What this means is that even though you can watch a video file on your computer, you likely cannot import all the frames into Krita. A warning will be displayed and inform you how many frames you can import with your current setup. #### Options ##### Document Options Only enabled when the import is into a new document. Width : Width of the new document. Height : Height of the new document. ##### Import Video Scale Width : The desired width in pixels Height : The desired height in pixels Filter : The filter to use for the resizing. ##### FFMpeg FFMpeg Path : Path to the ffmpeg executable, necessary for importing the video data. FFProbe path : Path to the ffmpeg probe executable, which is included with ffmpeg. This allows Krita to learn the video information from the file. See also [[1](#id3)] [The source for the libre pixel cup male walk cycle](https://opengameart.org/content/liberated-pixel-cup-lpc-base-assets-sprites-map-tiles) ## 本地配图清单
