title: 模块化像素动画：部件拆分、遮挡与局部逐帧
heading: 模块化像素动画：部件拆分、遮挡与局部逐帧
author: Pedro Medeiros (Saint11)
text:
# 模块化像素动画：部件拆分、遮挡与局部逐帧

按部件制作较大像素角色，利用遮挡隐藏接缝，并保留需要逐帧重画的部分。

## 原图与静态辅助图

![大怪物展示部件与遮挡；下方小人物说明小素材也可用但收益有限；机械臂和靴子示范关节材质与旋转连接。](../../assets/supplement/MAKE-025/Modular.gif)

![Modular.gif 第0帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/MAKE-025/Modular-frame-000.png)

![Modular.gif 第22帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/MAKE-025/Modular-frame-022.png)

![Modular.gif 第43帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/MAKE-025/Modular-frame-043.png)

## 读图

大怪物展示部件与遮挡；下方小人物说明小素材也可用但收益有限；机械臂和靴子示范关节材质与旋转连接。

## 根据原图整理的步骤

1. 先画整体草图，确认各部件如何组合及遮挡。
2. 单独制作部件，隐藏在其他部件后方的区域也需补完整。
3. 移动和旋转部件构建动作；并非所有部件都能免于逐帧动画。
4. 把需要弯曲的接缝藏到其他部件后，或用关节材质帮助解释连接处。
5. 机械部件可以加入多层与旋转点附近的细节；避免没有可见支点的旋转。

## 练习（整理者补充）

整理者练习：拆分一只两节机械臂，给旋转关节预留遮挡区域，并在几个关键角度检查像素旋转后的边缘。

## 验收（整理者补充）

- [ ] 隐藏部分有足够延展
- [ ] 关节没有裂缝
- [ ] 旋转点可被结构解释
- [ ] 需要逐帧修整的区域有记录

## 适用边界

部件旋转可能改变像素节奏；引擎实时变换与手工像素动画是不同取舍，不能自动宣称所有角度都保持像素完美。 原图为教学材料；不可把阅读或插入参考图说成已制作游戏美术。

## 来源与许可

作者Pedro Medeiros（Saint11），[固定来源](https://github.com/saint11/Saint11Tutorials/blob/ce1393eb2c46441d917134a9fd52e15575ee10a7/Modular.gif)。仓库[README许可声明](https://github.com/saint11/Saint11Tutorials/blob/ce1393eb2c46441d917134a9fd52e15575ee10a7/README.md)为[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)。原GIF保持原样；PNG为抽帧；中文为人工读图整理而非逐字OCR；练习与验收为整理者补充。新增内容继续按CC BY 4.0提供并保留原作者署名。

title: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
heading: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 用节点与场景组织像素游戏

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

先理解节点树和可保存场景，再把角色、房屋、道具拆成可独立编辑的单位。

## 前提

- 能打开 Godot 4.5 编辑器

## 中文操作路线

1. 在新场景中添加根节点，观察场景树、检查器与二维视图各自负责什么。
2. 按原文建立带文字的最小场景，修改节点属性并观察视图中的变化。
3. 把场景保存成 .tscn；分别运行当前场景和整个项目，确认两者入口不同。
4. 把一个场景设为主场景；练习把角色显示节点和碰撞节点放在同一角色根节点之下。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

建立一个名为 Village 的场景，以及独立的 Signpost 场景。先用文本占位验证结构，再替换成你自己的像素素材。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 运行项目时进入指定主场景。
- [ ] 节点名称能反映职责，显示与交互子节点归在正确父节点下。
- [ ] 能解释节点是组成单位、场景是保存后的节点树。

## 版本与边界

本篇属于引擎基础，不会直接教绘画；像素素材的尺寸与锚点应在美术规范中另行固定。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Nodes and Scenes

In [Overview of Godot's key concepts](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/getting_started/introduction/key_concepts_overview.html#doc-key-concepts-overview), we saw that a Godot game is a tree of
scenes and that each scene is a tree of nodes. In this lesson, we explain a bit
more about them. You will also create your first scene.

#### Nodes

**Nodes are the fundamental building blocks of your game**. They are like the
ingredients in a recipe. There are dozens of kinds that can display an image,
play a sound, represent a camera, and much more.

![原教程图示：Nodes — nodes_and_scenes_nodes.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_nodes.webp)

All nodes have the following characteristics:

- A name.
- Editable properties.
- They receive callbacks to update every frame.
- You can extend them with new properties and functions.
- You can add them to another node as a child.

title: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
heading: Nodes
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
The last characteristic is important. **Together, nodes form a tree**, which is a powerful
feature to organize projects. Since different nodes have different functions,
combining them produces more complex behavior. As we saw before, you can build a
playable character the camera follows using a [CharacterBody2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_characterbody2d.html#class-characterbody2d)
node, a [Sprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d) node,
a [Camera2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_camera2d.html#class-camera2d) node, and a [CollisionShape2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_collisionshape2d.html#class-collisionshape2d) node.

![原教程图示：Nodes — nodes_and_scenes_character_nodes.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_character_nodes.webp)

#### Scenes

When you organize nodes in a tree, like our character, we call this construct a
scene. Once saved, scenes work like new node types in the editor, where you can
add them as a child of an existing node. In that case, the instance of the scene
appears as a single node with its internals hidden.

Scenes allow you to structure your game's code however you want. You can
**compose nodes** to create custom and complex node types, like a game character
that runs and jumps, a life bar, a chest with which you can interact, and more.

![原教程图示：Scenes — nodes_and_scenes_3d_scene_example.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_3d_scene_example.webp)

The Godot editor essentially is a **scene editor**. It has plenty of tools for
editing 2D and 3D scenes, as well as user interfaces. A Godot project can
contain as many of these scenes as you need. The engine only requires one as
your application's **main scene**. This is the scene Godot will first load when
you or a player runs the game.

On top of acting like nodes, scenes have the following characteristics:

title: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
heading: Scenes
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
1. They always have one root node, like the "Player" in our example.
2. You can save them to your local drive and load them later.
3. You can create as many instances of a scene as you'd like. You could have
   five or ten characters in your game, created from your Character scene.

#### Creating your first scene

Let's create our first scene with a single node. To do so, you will need to
[create a new project](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/editor/project_manager.html#doc-creating-and-importing-projects) first. After
opening the project, you should see an empty editor.

![原教程图示：Creating your first scene — nodes_and_scenes_01_empty_editor.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_01_empty_editor.webp)

In an empty scene, the Scene dock on the left shows several options to add a
root node quickly. 2D Scene adds a [Node2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_node2d.html#class-node2d) node,
3D Scene adds a [Node3D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_node3d.html#class-node3d) node,
and User Interface adds a [Control](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_control.html#class-control) node.
These presets are here for convenience; they are not mandatory.
Other Node lets you select any node to be the root node.
In an empty scene, Other Node is equivalent to pressing the Add Child Node
button at the top-left of the Scene dock, which usually adds
a new node as a child of the currently selected node.

We're going to add a single [Label](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_label.html#class-label) node to our scene. Its function is to draw
text on the screen.

Press the Add Child Node button or Other Node to create a
root node.

![原教程图示：Creating your first scene — nodes_and_scenes_02_scene_dock.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_02_scene_dock.webp)

The Create New Node dialog opens, showing the long list of available nodes.

![原教程图示：Creating your first scene — nodes_and_scenes_03_create_node_window.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_03_create_node_window.webp)

Select the Label node. You can type its name to filter down the list.

title: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
heading: Creating your first scene
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Creating your first scene — nodes_and_scenes_04_create_label_window.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_04_create_label_window.webp)

Click on the Label node to select it and click the Create button at
the bottom of the window.

![原教程图示：Creating your first scene — nodes_and_scenes_05_editor_with_label.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_05_editor_with_label.webp)

A lot happens when you add a scene's first node. The scene changes to the 2D
workspace because Label is a 2D node type. The Label appears, selected, in the
top-left corner of the viewport. The node appears in the Scene dock on the left,
and the node's properties appear in the Inspector dock on the right.

#### Changing a node's properties

The next step is to change the Label's Text property. Let's change
it to "Hello World".

Head to the Inspector dock on the right of the viewport. Click inside the field
below the Text property and type "Hello World".

![原教程图示：Changing a node's properties — nodes_and_scenes_06_label_text.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_06_label_text.webp)

You will see the text draw in the viewport as you type.

See also

You can edit any property listed in the Inspector as we did with
the Text. For a complete reference of the Inspector dock, see
[Inspector Dock](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/editor/inspector_dock.html#doc-editor-inspector-dock).

You can move your Label node in the viewport by selecting the move tool in the
toolbar.

![原教程图示：Changing a node's properties — nodes_and_scenes_07_move_tool.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_07_move_tool.webp)

With the Label selected, click and drag anywhere in the viewport to
move it to the center of the view delimited by the rectangle.

![原教程图示：Changing a node's properties — nodes_and_scenes_08_hello_world_text.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_08_hello_world_text.webp)

#### Running the scene

Everything's ready to run the scene! Press the Run Current Scene
button in the top-right of the screen or press `F6` (`Cmd + R` on
macOS).

title: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
heading: Running the scene
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Running the scene — nodes_and_scenes_09_play_scene_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_09_play_scene_button.webp)

A popup invites you to save the scene, which is required to run it. Click the
Save button in the file browser to save it as `label.tscn`.

![原教程图示：Running the scene — nodes_and_scenes_10_save_scene_as.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_10_save_scene_as.webp)

Note

The Save Scene As dialog, like other file dialogs in the editor, only
allows you to save files inside the project. The `res://` path at
the top of the window represents the project's root directory and
stands for "resource path". For more information about file paths in
Godot, see [File system](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/filesystem.html#doc-filesystem).

The application should open in a new window and display the text "Hello World".

![原教程图示：Running the scene — nodes_and_scenes_11_final_result.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_11_final_result.webp)

Close the window or press `F8` (`Cmd + .` on macOS) to quit the running scene.

#### Setting the main scene

To run our test scene, we used the Run Current Scene button. Another button
next to it, Run Project, allows you to set and run the project's
**main scene**. You can also press `F5` (`Cmd + B` on macOS) to do so.

![原教程图示：Setting the main scene — nodes_and_scenes_12_play_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_12_play_button.webp)

Note

Running the project's *main scene* is distinct from running the
*current scene*. If you encounter unexpected behavior, check
to ensure you are running the correct scene.

A popup window appears and invites you to select the main scene.

![原教程图示：Setting the main scene — nodes_and_scenes_13_main_scene_popup.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_13_main_scene_popup.webp)

Click the Select button, and in the file dialog that appears, double
click on `label.tscn`.

![原教程图示：Setting the main scene — nodes_and_scenes_14_select_main_scene.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-001/nodes_and_scenes_14_select_main_scene.webp)

title: 用节点与场景组织像素游戏
heading: Setting the main scene
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
The demo should run again. Moving forward, every time you run the project, Godot
will use this scene as a starting point.

Note

The editor saves the main scene's path in a project.godot file in your
project's directory. While you can edit this text file directly to
change project settings, you can also use the Project > Project Settings
window to do so. For more information, see [Project Settings](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/editor/project_settings.html#doc-project-settings).

In the next part, we will discuss another key concept in games and in Godot:
creating instances of a scene.

---

heading: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

掌握同一场景多个实例的共性与局部覆盖，避免复制节点后难以批量维护。

## 前提

- DEV-001

## 中文操作路线

1. 下载并打开原文的实例化练习项目，观察主场景如何引用独立的球场景。
2. 在主场景中放置多个同源实例，移动位置并运行检查。
3. 打开源场景修改共享属性，回到主场景观察所有实例的更新。
4. 对一个实例单独覆盖属性，再用恢复按钮取消覆盖；理解源场景值与实例值的区别。
5. 把同样方法用于树木或路灯：共用素材与交互结构，仅覆盖位置、颜色或交互参数。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

用一个 Tree.tscn 放置六棵树，统一修改树冠图层，再只改变其中一棵树的交互半径。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 源场景变化能传播到未覆盖该属性的实例。
- [ ] 局部覆盖不影响其他实例。
- [ ] 重复物件没有被维护成六份互不关联的节点树。

## 版本与边界

原文用物理小球演示复用；树木案例是整理者的迁移练习，并非原教程原图。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Creating instances

Note

This tutorial refers to instancing scenes in the editor. To learn how
to instance scenes from code, see [Nodes and scene instances](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/nodes_and_scene_instances.html#doc-nodes-and-scene-instances).

Godot's approach to *instancing* described below should not be confused with
hardware instancing that can be used to render large amounts of similar
objects quickly. See [Optimization using MultiMeshes](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/performance/using_multimesh.html#doc-using-multimesh) instead.

In the previous part, we saw that a scene is a collection of nodes organized in
a tree structure, with a single node as its root. You can split your project
into any number of scenes. This feature helps you break down and organize your
game's different components.

You can create as many scenes as you'd like and save them as files with the
`.tscn` extension, which stands for "text scene". The `label.tscn` file from
the previous lesson was an example. We call those files "Packed Scenes" as they
pack information about your scene's content.

title: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
heading: Creating instances
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Here's an example of a ball. It's composed of a [RigidBody2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_rigidbody2d.html#class-rigidbody2d) node as its root named Ball, which allows the ball to fall
and bounce on walls, a [Sprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d) node, and a
[CollisionShape2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_collisionshape2d.html#class-collisionshape2d).

![原教程图示：Creating instances — instancing_ball_scene.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_ball_scene.webp)

Once you have saved a scene, it works as a blueprint: you can reproduce it in other
scenes as many times as you'd like. Replicating an object from a template like
this is called **instancing**.

![原教程图示：Creating instances — instancing_ball_instances_example.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_ball_instances_example.webp)

As we mentioned in the previous part, instanced scenes behave like a node: the
editor hides their content by default. When you instance the Ball, you only see
the Ball node. Notice also how each duplicate has a unique name.

Every instance of the Ball scene starts with the same structure and properties
as `ball.tscn`. However, you can modify each independently, such as changing
how they bounce, how heavy they are, or any property exposed by the source
scene.

#### In practice

Let's use instancing in practice to see how it works in Godot. We invite
you to download the ball's sample project we prepared for you:
[instancing_starter.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs-project-starters/releases/download/latest-4.x/instancing_starter.zip).

Extract the archive on your computer. To import it, you need the Project Manager.
The Project Manager is accessed by opening Godot, or if you already have Godot
opened, click on Project > Quit to Project List (`Ctrl + Shift + Q`, `Ctrl + Option + Cmd + Q` on macOS)

In the Project Manager, click the Import button to import the project.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_import_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_import_button.webp)

title: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
heading: In practice
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
In the pop-up that appears navigate to the folder you extracted.
Double-click the `project.godot` file to open it.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_import_project_file.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_import_project_file.webp)

Finally, click the Import button.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_import_and_edit_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_import_and_edit_button.webp)

A window notifying you that the project was last opened in an older Godot version
may appear, that's not an issue. Click Ok to open the project.

The project contains two packed scenes: `main.tscn`, containing walls against
which the ball collides, and `ball.tscn`. The Main scene should open
automatically. If you're seeing an empty 3D scene instead of the main scene, click the 2D button at the top of the screen.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_2d_scene_select.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_2d_scene_select.webp)
![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_main_scene.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_main_scene.webp)

Let's add a ball as a child of the Main node. In the Scene dock, select the Main
node. Then, click the link icon at the top of the scene dock. This button allows
you to add an instance of a scene as a child of the currently selected node.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_scene_link_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_scene_link_button.webp)

Double-click the ball scene to instance it.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_instance_child_window.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_instance_child_window.webp)

The ball appears in the top-left corner of the viewport.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_ball_instanced.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_ball_instanced.webp)

Click on it and drag it towards the center of the view.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_ball_moved.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_ball_moved.webp)

Play the game by pressing `F5` (`Cmd + B` on macOS). You should see it fall.

title: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
heading: In practice
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Now, we want to create more instances of the Ball node. With the ball still
selected, press `Ctrl + D` (`Cmd + D` on macOS) to call the duplicate
command. Click and drag to move the new ball to a different location.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_ball_duplicated.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_ball_duplicated.webp)

You can repeat this process until you have several in the scene.

![原教程图示：In practice — instancing_main_scene_with_balls.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_main_scene_with_balls.webp)

Play the game again. You should now see every ball fall independently from one
another. This is what instances do. Each is an independent reproduction of a
template scene.

#### Editing scenes and instances

There is more to instances. With this feature, you can:

1. Change the properties of one ball without affecting the others using the
   Inspector.
2. Change the default properties of every Ball by opening the `ball.tscn` scene
   and making a change to the Ball node there. Upon saving, all instances of the
   Ball in the project will see their values update.

Note

Changing a property on an instance always overrides values from the
corresponding packed scene.

Let's try this. Double-click `ball.tscn` in the FileSystem to open it.

![原教程图示：Editing scenes and instances — instancing_ball_scene_open.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_ball_scene_open.webp)

In the Scene dock on the left, select the Ball node. Then, in the Inspector on the
right, click on the PhysicsMaterial property to expand it.

![原教程图示：Editing scenes and instances — instancing_physics_material_expand.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_physics_material_expand.webp)

Set its Bounce property to `0.5` by clicking on the number field, typing `0.5`,
and pressing `Enter`.

![原教程图示：Editing scenes and instances — instancing_property_bounce_updated.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_property_bounce_updated.webp)

title: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
heading: Editing scenes and instances
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Play the game by pressing `F5` (`Cmd + B` on macOS) and notice how all balls now bounce a lot
more. As the Ball scene is a template for all instances, modifying it and saving
causes all instances to update accordingly.

Let's now adjust an individual instance. Head back to the Main scene by clicking
on the corresponding tab above the viewport.

![原教程图示：Editing scenes and instances — instancing_scene_tabs.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_scene_tabs.webp)

Select one of the instanced Ball nodes and, in the Inspector, set its
Gravity Scale value to `10`.

![原教程图示：Editing scenes and instances — instancing_property_gravity_scale.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_property_gravity_scale.png)

A grey "revert" button appears next to the adjusted property.

![原教程图示：Editing scenes and instances — instancing_property_revert_icon.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_property_revert_icon.png)

This icon indicates you are overriding a value from the source packed scene.
Even if you modify the property in the original scene, the value override will
be preserved in the instance. Clicking the revert icon will restore the
property to the value in the saved scene.

Rerun the game and notice how this ball now falls much faster than the others.

Note

You may notice you are unable to change the values of the PhysicsMaterial
of the ball. This is because PhysicsMaterial is a *resource*, and needs
to be made unique before you can edit it in a scene that is linking to its
original scene. To make a resource unique for one instance, right-click on
the Physics Material property in the Inspector and click Make Unique
in the context menu.

Resources are another essential building block of Godot games we will cover
in a later lesson.

#### Scene instances as a design language

Instances and scenes in Godot offer an excellent design language, setting the
engine apart from others out there. We designed Godot around this concept from
the ground up.

title: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
heading: Scene instances as a design language
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
We recommend dismissing architectural code patterns when making games with
Godot, such as Model-View-Controller (MVC) or Entity-Relationship diagrams.
Instead, you can start by imagining the elements players will see in your game
and structure your code around them.

For example, you could break down a shooter game like so:

![原教程图示：Scene instances as a design language — instancing_diagram_shooter.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_diagram_shooter.png)

You can come up with a diagram like this for almost any type of game. Each
rectangle represents an entity that's visible in the game from the player's
perspective. The arrows point towards the instantiator of each scene.

Once you have a diagram, we recommend creating a scene for each element listed
in it to develop your game. You'll use instancing, either by code or directly in
the editor, to build your tree of scenes.

Programmers tend to spend a lot of time designing abstract architectures and
trying to fit components into it. Designing based on scenes makes development
faster and more straightforward, allowing you to focus on the game logic itself.
Because most game components map directly to a scene, using a design based on
scene instantiation means you need little other architectural code.

Here's the example of a scene diagram for an open-world game with tons of assets
and nested elements:

![原教程图示：Scene instances as a design language — instancing_diagram_open_world.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-002/instancing_diagram_open_world.png)

Imagine we started by creating the room. We could make a couple of different
room scenes, with unique arrangements of furniture in them. Later, we could make
a house scene that uses multiple room instances for the interior. We would
create a citadel out of many instanced houses and a large terrain on which we
would place the citadel. Each of these would be a scene instancing one or more sub-scenes.

Later, we could create scenes representing guards and add them to the citadel.
They would be indirectly added to the overall game world.

title: 用场景实例复用树木、建筑和道具
heading: Scene instances as a design language
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
With Godot, it's easy to iterate on your game like this, as all you need to do
is create and instantiate more scenes. We designed the editor to be accessible
to programmers, designers, and artists alike. A typical team development process
can involve 2D or 3D artists, level designers, game designers, and animators,
all working with the Godot editor.

#### Summary

Instancing, the process of producing an object from a blueprint, has many handy
uses. With scenes, it gives you:

- The ability to divide your game into reusable components.
- A tool to structure and encapsulate complex systems.
- A language to think about your game project's structure in a natural way.

---

title: 读取玩家输入并驱动角色
heading: 读取玩家输入并驱动角色
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 读取玩家输入并驱动角色

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

从按键状态读取开始，将输入、方向与运动参数连接起来。

## 前提

- 会给节点附加脚本
- 理解变量和函数

## 中文操作路线

1. 先运行原文已有旋转与前进脚本，确认每帧更新发生的位置。
2. 使用 Input.is_action_pressed 读取动作，而非把按键编码散落在各处。
3. 把左、右动作转成旋转方向，再将向前动作与当前朝向结合。
4. 检查同时按键、松开按键以及没有输入时的行为；保留 delta 对每秒速度的换算。
5. 俯视四向或八向移动改用 DEV-012 的 Input.get_vector 路线，不要把旋转式控制直接等同于四向角色。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

为原示例添加暂停运动动作，要求松开移动键后停止前进，但仍能按方向键旋转。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 输入动作名称与项目设置完全相同。
- [ ] 松开按键后没有残留速度。
- [ ] 改变运行帧率时，按住一秒得到的运动量基本一致。

## 版本与边界

本篇示范旋转式运动；角色碰撞响应需要另外阅读 CharacterBody2D 教程。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Listening to player input

Building upon the previous lesson, [Creating your first script](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/getting_started/step_by_step/scripting_first_script.html#doc-scripting-first-script), let's look
at another important feature of any game: giving control to the player.
To add this, we need to modify our `sprite_2d.gd` code.

![原教程图示：Listening to player input — scripting_first_script_moving_with_input.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-003/scripting_first_script_moving_with_input.gif)

You have two main tools to process the player's input in Godot:

1. The built-in input callbacks, mainly `_unhandled_input()`. Like
   `_process()`, it's a built-in virtual function that Godot calls every time
   the player presses a key. It's the tool you want to use to react to events
   that don't happen every frame, like pressing `Space` to jump. To learn
   more about input callbacks, see [Using InputEvent](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/inputs/inputevent.html#doc-inputevent).
2. The `Input` singleton. A singleton is a globally accessible object. Godot
   provides access to several in scripts. It's the right tool to check for input
   every frame.

We're going to use the `Input` singleton here as we need to know if the player
wants to turn or move every frame.

title: 读取玩家输入并驱动角色
heading: Listening to player input
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community

title: 读取玩家输入并驱动角色
heading: Listening to player input
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
This will ignore the code that moved the icon's position in a circle without user input from the previous exercise.

If you run the scene with this code, the icon should rotate when you press
`Left` and `Right`.

#### Moving when pressing "up"

To only move when pressing a key, we need to modify the code that calculates the
velocity. Uncomment the code and replace the line starting with `var velocity` with the code below.

```gdscript
var velocity = Vector2.ZERO
if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
    velocity = Vector2.UP.rotated(rotation) * speed
```

```csharp
var velocity = Vector2.Zero;
if (Input.IsActionPressed("ui_up"))
{
    velocity = Vector2.Up.Rotated(Rotation) * _speed;
}
```

We initialize the `velocity` with a value of `Vector2.ZERO`, another
constant of the built-in `Vector` type representing a 2D vector of length 0.

If the player presses the "ui_up" action, we then update the velocity's value,
causing the sprite to move forward.

#### Complete script

Here is the complete `sprite_2d.gd` file for reference.

```gdscript
extends Sprite2D

var speed = 400
var angular_speed = PI


func _process(delta):
    var direction = 0
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_left"):
        direction = -1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_right"):
        direction = 1

    rotation += angular_speed * direction * delta

    var velocity = Vector2.ZERO
    if Input.is_action_pressed("ui_up"):
        velocity = Vector2.UP.rotated(rotation) * speed

    position += velocity * delta
```

heading: 用信号连接按钮、计时器与游戏事件
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 用信号连接按钮、计时器与游戏事件

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

学习编辑器连线和代码连接两种信号方式，让按钮、计时器和自定义事件触发逻辑。

## 前提

- DEV-001
- 基础 GDScript

## 中文操作路线

1. 按原文搭建按钮与移动图像的场景，选中按钮并打开信号面板。
2. 把 pressed 信号连接到接收节点的方法，在回调中切换运动。
3. 添加 Timer 并以代码连接 timeout，比较信号声明、连接和响应的不同职责。
4. 阅读完整脚本后创建自定义信号，把事件的必要数据作为参数传递。
5. 迁移到俯视场景时，让宝箱发出 opened 或 collected 信号，由关卡或背包系统接收。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

建立一个可点击的宝箱占位场景，第一次开启时发出包含道具名称的信号；第二次点击不重复发放。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 事件发出一次时接收函数只执行一次。
- [ ] 信号参数与接收函数一致。
- [ ] 宝箱场景不依赖某个固定 HUD 节点路径。

## 版本与边界

opened 等命名是整理者练习设计；官方原文以按钮和计时器示范。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Using signals

In this lesson, we will look at signals. They are messages that nodes emit when
something specific happens to them, like a button being pressed. Other nodes can
connect to that signal and call a function when the event occurs.

Signals are a delegation mechanism built into Godot that allows one game object to
react to a change in another without them referencing one another. Using signals
limits [coupling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coupling_(computer_programming)) and keeps your
code flexible.

For example, you might have a life bar on the screen that represents the
player's health. When the player takes damage or uses a healing potion, you want
the bar to reflect the change. To do so, in Godot, you would use signals.

Like methods ([Callable](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_callable.html#class-callable)), signals are a first-class type since Godot
4.0. This means you can pass them around as method arguments directly without
having to pass them as strings, which allows for better autocompletion and is
less error-prone. See the [Signal](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_signal.html#class-signal) class reference for a list of
what you can do with the Signal type directly.

See also

title: 用信号连接按钮、计时器与游戏事件
heading: Using signals
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
As mentioned in the introduction, signals are Godot's version of the
observer pattern. You can learn more about it in
[Game Programming Patterns](https://gameprogrammingpatterns.com/observer.html).

We will now use a signal to make our Godot icon from the previous lesson
([Listening to player input](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/getting_started/step_by_step/scripting_player_input.html#doc-scripting-player-input)) move and stop by pressing a button.

Note

For this project, we will be following the Godot naming conventions.

- **GDScript**: Classes (nodes) use PascalCase, variables and
  functions use snake_case, and constants use ALL_CAPS (See
  [GDScript style guide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_styleguide.html#doc-gdscript-styleguide)).
- **C#**: Classes, export variables and methods use PascalCase,
  private fields use _camelCase, local variables and parameters use
  camelCase (See [C# style guide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_style_guide.html#doc-c-sharp-styleguide)). Be careful to type
  the method names precisely when connecting signals.

#### Scene setup

To add a button to our game, we will create a new scene which will include
both a [Button](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_button.html#class-button) and the `sprite_2d.tscn` scene we created in
the [Creating your first script](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/getting_started/step_by_step/scripting_first_script.html#doc-scripting-first-script) lesson.

Create a new scene by going to the menu Scene > New Scene.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_01_new_scene.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_01_new_scene.webp)

In the Scene dock, click the 2D Scene button. This will add
a [Node2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_node2d.html#class-node2d) as our root.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_02_2d_scene.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_02_2d_scene.webp)

In the FileSystem dock, click and drag the `sprite_2d.tscn` file you saved
previously onto the Node2D to instantiate it.

title: 用信号连接按钮、计时器与游戏事件
heading: Scene setup
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_03_dragging_scene.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_03_dragging_scene.png)

We want to add another node as a sibling of the Sprite2D. To do so, right-click
on Node2D and select Add Child Node.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_04_add_child_node.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_04_add_child_node.webp)

Search for the [Button](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_button.html#class-button) node and add it.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_05_add_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_05_add_button.webp)

The node is small by default. Click and drag on the bottom-right handle of the
Button in the viewport to resize it.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_06_drag_button.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_06_drag_button.png)

If you don't see the handles, ensure the select tool is active in the toolbar.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_07_select_tool.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_07_select_tool.webp)

Click and drag on the button itself to move it closer to the sprite.

You can also write a label on the Button by editing its Text property
in the Inspector. Enter `Toggle motion`.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_08_toggle_motion_text.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_08_toggle_motion_text.webp)

Your scene tree and viewport should look like this.

![原教程图示：Scene setup — signals_09_scene_setup.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_09_scene_setup.png)

Save your newly created scene as `node_2d.tscn`, if you haven't already.
You can then run it with `F6` (`Cmd + R` on macOS).
At the moment, the button will be visible, but nothing will happen if you
press it.

#### Connecting a signal in the editor

Here, we want to connect the Button's "pressed" signal to our Sprite2D, and we
want to call a new function that will toggle its motion on and off. We need to
have a script attached to the Sprite2D node, which we do from the previous
lesson.

You can connect signals in the Node dock. Select the Button node and, on the
right side of the editor, click on the tab named Node next to the
Inspector.

title: 用信号连接按钮、计时器与游戏事件
heading: Connecting a signal in the editor
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Connecting a signal in the editor — signals_10_node_dock.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_10_node_dock.webp)

The dock displays a list of signals available on the selected node.

![原教程图示：Connecting a signal in the editor — signals_11_pressed_signals.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_11_pressed_signals.webp)

Double-click the "pressed" signal to open the node connection window.

![原教程图示：Connecting a signal in the editor — signals_12_node_connection.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_12_node_connection.webp)

There, you can connect the signal to the Sprite2D node. The node needs a
receiver method, a function that Godot will call when the Button emits the
signal. The editor generates one for you. By convention, we name these callback
methods "_on_node_name_signal_name". Here, it'll be "_on_button_pressed".

Note

When connecting signals via the editor's Node dock, you can use two
modes. The simple one only allows you to connect to nodes that have a
script attached to them and creates a new callback function on them.

![原教程图示：Connecting a signal in the editor — signals_advanced_connection_window.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_advanced_connection_window.png)

The advanced view lets you connect to any node and any built-in
function, add arguments to the callback, and set options. You can
toggle the mode in the window's bottom-right by clicking the Advanced
button.

Note

If you are using an external editor (such as VS Code), this
automatic code generation might not work. In this case, you need to connect
the signal via code as explained in the next section.

Click the Connect button to complete the signal connection and jump to the
Script workspace. You should see the new method with a connection icon in the
left margin.

![原教程图示：Connecting a signal in the editor — signals_13_signals_connection_icon.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-004/signals_13_signals_connection_icon.webp)

If you click the icon, a window pops up and displays information about the
connection. This feature is only available when connecting nodes in the editor.

title: 用信号连接按钮、计时器与游戏事件
heading: Summary
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Signals have many uses. With them, you can react to a node entering or exiting
the game world, to a collision, to a character entering or leaving an area, to
an element of the interface changing size, and much more.

For example, an [Area2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_area2d.html#class-area2d) representing a coin emits a
`body_entered` signal whenever the player's physics body enters its collision
shape, allowing you to know when the player collected it.

In the next section, [Your first 2D game](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/getting_started/first_2d_game/index.html#doc-your-first-2d-game), you'll create a complete 2D
game and put everything you learned so far into practice.

text:
# 完整二维小游戏：项目与素材准备

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

开始官方 Dodge the Creeps 项目，建立资源目录、窗口设置和素材导入基础。

## 前提

- 完成 Godot 基础节点与脚本入门

## 中文操作路线

1. 新建项目，并按原文要求准备官方教学资源包。
2. 把资源解压到项目目录，等待编辑器导入后确认目录和资源名称。
3. 设置项目的窗口尺寸与拉伸参数，区分设计分辨率和实际窗口大小。
4. 把场景、脚本与素材按职责分开存放，再保存项目设置。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

建立项目目录清单，注明角色、敌人、字体、声音各自在哪里；保留原包的许可信息。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 素材导入没有丢失纹理或字体。
- [ ] 窗口方向和尺寸符合原教程。
- [ ] 后续章节引用资源时能定位到相同文件名。

## 版本与边界

官方项目的素材不是严格像素画，也不是俯视 RPG；这里学习完整游戏结构，像素清晰度另见 DEV-021。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Setting up the project

In this short first part, we'll set up and organize the project.

Launch Godot and create a new project.

![原教程图示：Setting up the project — new-project-button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-005/new-project-button.webp)

When creating the new project, you only need to choose a valid *Project Path*. You can leave the other default settings alone.

Download [dodge_the_creeps_2d_assets.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs-project-starters/releases/download/latest-4.x/dodge_the_creeps_2d_assets.zip).
The archive contains the images and sounds you'll be using
to make the game. Extract the archive and move the `art/`
and `fonts/` directories to your project's directory.

Download [dodge_the_creeps_2d_assets.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs-project-starters/releases/download/latest-4.x/dodge_the_creeps_2d_assets.zip).
The archive contains the images and sounds you'll be using
to make the game. Extract the archive and move the `art/`
and `fonts/` directories to your project's directory.

Ensure that you have the required dependencies to use C# in Godot.
You need the latest stable .NET SDK, and an editor such as VS Code.
See [Prerequisites](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_basics.html#doc-c-sharp-setup).

The C++ part of this tutorial wasn't rewritten for the new GDExtension system yet.

Your project folder should look like this.

title: 完整二维小游戏：项目与素材准备
heading: Setting up the project
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Setting up the project — folder-content.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-005/folder-content.webp)

This game is designed for portrait mode, so we need to adjust the size of the
game window. Click on *Project -> Project Settings* to open the project settings
window, in the left column open the *Display -> Window* tab. There, set
"Viewport Width" to `480` and "Viewport Height" to `720`. You can see the
"Project" menu on the upper left corner.

![原教程图示：Setting up the project — setting-project-width-and-height.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-005/setting-project-width-and-height.webp)

Also, under the **Stretch** options, set **Mode** to `canvas_items` and **Aspect** to `keep`.
This ensures that the game scales consistently on different sized screens.

![原教程图示：Setting up the project — setting-stretch-mode.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-005/setting-stretch-mode.webp)

#### Organizing the project

In this project, we will make 3 independent scenes: `Player`, `Mob`, and
`HUD`, which we will combine into the game's `Main` scene.

In a larger project, it might be useful to create folders to hold the various
scenes and their scripts, but for this relatively small game, you can save your
scenes and scripts in the project's root folder, identified by `res://`. You
can see your project folders in the FileSystem dock in the lower left corner:

![原教程图示：Organizing the project — filesystem_dock.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-005/filesystem_dock.webp)

With the project in place, we're ready to design the player scene in the next lesson.

title: 完整二维小游戏：玩家场景与动画资源
heading: 完整二维小游戏：玩家场景与动画资源
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 完整二维小游戏：玩家场景与动画资源

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

组合 Area2D、动画精灵与碰撞形状，制作可独立复用的玩家场景。

## 前提

- DEV-005

## 中文操作路线

1. 以 Area2D 建立玩家根节点，并按原文配置命名与分组方式。
2. 添加 AnimatedSprite2D，为 SpriteFrames 创建行走方向相关的动画。
3. 把素材帧放入正确动画并设置速度，使用编辑器预览播放。
4. 添加 CollisionShape2D，选择适合角色的形状并调整大小。
5. 保存玩家场景，确认它可以独立打开和后续被主场景实例化。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

为玩家准备一个额外 idle 动画，记录它与原行走帧共享的画布尺寸和底部锚点。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 动画帧没有因裁剪导致角色跳动。
- [ ] 碰撞形状覆盖实际接触区域。
- [ ] 节点名称与下一章脚本引用一致。

## 版本与边界

原教程玩家使用 Area2D 做重叠检测；需要撞墙和沿墙滑动的 RPG 玩家通常改用 CharacterBody2D。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Creating the player scene

With the project settings in place, we can start working on the
player-controlled character.

The first scene will define the `Player` object. One of the benefits of
creating a separate Player scene is that we can test it separately, even before
we've created other parts of the game.

#### Node structure

To begin, we need to choose a root node for the player object. As a general
rule, a scene's root node should reflect the object's desired functionality -
what the object *is*. In the upper-left corner, in the "Scene" tab, click the
"Other Node" button and add an [Area2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_area2d.html#class-area2d) node to the scene.

![原教程图示：Node structure — add_node.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/add_node.webp)

When you add the `Area2D` node, Godot will display the following **warning icon**
next to it in the scene tree:

![原教程图示：Node structure — no_shape_warning.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/no_shape_warning.webp)

This warning tells us that the `Area2D` node requires a shape to detect collisions or overlaps.
We can **ignore the warning temporarily** because we will first set up the player's visuals
(using an animated sprite). Once the visuals are ready, we will add a collision shape as a child
node. This will allow us to accurately size and position the shape based on the sprite's appearance.

title: 完整二维小游戏：玩家场景与动画资源
heading: Node structure
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
With `Area2D` we can detect objects that overlap or run into the player.
Change the node's name to `Player` by double-clicking on it. Now that we've
set the scene's root node, we can add additional nodes to give it more
functionality.

Before we add any children to the `Player` node, we want to make sure we don't
accidentally move or resize them by clicking on them. Select the node and click
the icon to the right of the lock. Its tooltip says "Groups the selected node
with its children. This causes the parent to be selected when any child
node is clicked in 2D and 3D view."

![原教程图示：Node structure — lock_children.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/lock_children.webp)

Save the scene as `player.tscn`. Click **Scene > Save**, or press `Ctrl + S`
on Windows/Linux or `Cmd + S` on macOS.

Note

For this project, we will be following the Godot naming conventions.

- **GDScript**: Classes (nodes) use PascalCase, variables and
  functions use snake_case, and constants use ALL_CAPS (See
  [GDScript style guide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/gdscript/gdscript_styleguide.html#doc-gdscript-styleguide)).
- **C#**: Classes, export variables and methods use PascalCase,
  private fields use _camelCase, local variables and parameters use
  camelCase (See [C# style guide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/scripting/c_sharp/c_sharp_style_guide.html#doc-c-sharp-styleguide)). Be careful to type
  the method names precisely when connecting signals.

#### Sprite animation

title: 完整二维小游戏：玩家场景与动画资源
heading: Sprite animation
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Click on the `Player` node and add (`Ctrl + A` on Windows/Linux or
`Cmd + A` on macOS) a child node [AnimatedSprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animatedsprite2d.html#class-animatedsprite2d). The `AnimatedSprite2D` will handle the
appearance and animations for our player. Notice that there is a warning symbol
next to the node. An `AnimatedSprite2D` requires a [SpriteFrames](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_spriteframes.html#class-spriteframes) resource, which is a list of the animations it can
display. Make sure `AnimatedSprite2D` is selected and then find the `Sprite Frames` property under
the `Animation` section in the Inspector and click "[empty]" -> "New SpriteFrames":

![原教程图示：Sprite animation — new_spriteframes.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/new_spriteframes.webp)

Click on the `SpriteFrames` you just created to open the "SpriteFrames" panel:

![原教程图示：Sprite animation — spriteframes_panel.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/spriteframes_panel.webp)

On the left is a list of animations. Click the `default` one and rename it to
`walk`. Then click the **Add Animation** button to create a second animation
named `up`.

Find the player images in the FileSystem dock - they're in the `art` folder
you unzipped earlier. Drag the two images for each animation, into the
**Animation Frames** side of the panel for the corresponding animation:

- `playerGrey_walk1` and `playerGrey_walk2` for the `walk` animation
- `playerGrey_up1` and `playerGrey_up2` for the `up` animation

![原教程图示：Sprite animation — spriteframes_panel2.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/spriteframes_panel2.webp)

The player images are a bit too large for the game window, so we need to scale
them down. Click on the `AnimatedSprite2D` node and set the `Scale` property
to `(0.5, 0.5)`. You can find it in the Inspector under the `Node2D`
heading.

![原教程图示：Sprite animation — player_scale.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/player_scale.webp)

title: 完整二维小游戏：玩家场景与动画资源
heading: Sprite animation
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Finally, add a [CollisionShape2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_collisionshape2d.html#class-collisionshape2d) as a child of
`Player`. This will determine the player's "hitbox", or the bounds of its
collision area. For this character, a `CapsuleShape2D` node gives the best
fit, so next to "Shape" in the Inspector, click "[empty]" -> "New
CapsuleShape2D". Using the two size handles, resize the shape to cover the
sprite:

![原教程图示：Sprite animation — player_coll_shape.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/player_coll_shape.webp)

When you're finished, your `Player` scene should look like this:

![原教程图示：Sprite animation — player_scene_nodes.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-006/player_scene_nodes.webp)

Once this is done, the warning on the `Area2D` node will disappear, as it now has
a shape assigned and can interact with other objects.

Make sure to save the scene again after these changes.

In the next part, we'll add a script to the player node to move and animate it.
Then, we'll set up collision detection to know when the player got hit by
something.

title: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
heading: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

把输入、速度、屏幕边界、动画和受击信号接成一个可测试的玩家控制器。

## 前提

- DEV-006
- 理解信号

## 中文操作路线

1. 给玩家添加脚本并定义速度，读取各方向输入形成运动向量。
2. 对非零方向进行归一化，再乘以速度与 delta，防止对角移动更快。
3. 根据移动方向播放动画与翻转图像；没有移动时停止动画。
4. 限制玩家位置在可见范围内，避免角色完全离开屏幕。
5. 连接碰撞信号，隐藏玩家并延迟禁用碰撞形状；通过 start 方法恢复初始位置与状态。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

在四个方向和四个对角方向各移动相同时间，记录距离；受击后重开一局确认可再次控制。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 斜向移动没有比轴向移动快。
- [ ] 站立时不会持续播放跑动帧。
- [ ] 重开时玩家显示、位置和碰撞均恢复。

## 版本与边界

Area2D 的这套直接位置更新不提供实体阻挡；切换到角色物理体后应采用 DEV-014 的运动方法。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Coding the player

In this lesson, we'll add player movement, animation, and set it up to detect
collisions.

To do so, we need to add some functionality that we can't get from a built-in
node, so we'll add a script. Click the `Player` node and click the "Attach
Script" button:

![原教程图示：Coding the player — add_script_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/add_script_button.webp)

In the script settings window, you can leave the default settings alone. Just
click "Create":

Note

If you're creating a C# script or other languages, select the language
from the language drop down menu before hitting create.

![原教程图示：Coding the player — attach_node_window.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/attach_node_window.webp)

Note

If this is your first time encountering GDScript, please read
[Scripting languages](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/getting_started/step_by_step/scripting_languages.html#doc-scripting) before continuing.

Start by declaring the member variables this object will need:

```gdscript
extends Area2D

@export var speed = 400 # How fast the player will move (pixels/sec).
var screen_size # Size of the game window.
```

```csharp
using Godot;

public partial class Player : Area2D
{
    [Export]
    public int Speed { get; set; } = 400; // How fast the player will move (pixels/sec).

    public Vector2 ScreenSize; // Size of the game window.
}
```

title: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
heading: Coding the player
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Using the `export` keyword on the first variable `speed` allows us to set
its value in the Inspector. This can be handy for values that you want to be
able to adjust just like a node's built-in properties. Click on the `Player`
node and you'll see the property now appears in the Inspector in a new section
with the name of the script. Remember, if you change the value here, it will
override the value written in the script.

Warning

If you're using C#, you need to (re)build the project assemblies
whenever you want to see new export variables or signals. This
build can be manually triggered by clicking the **Build** button at
the top right of the editor.

![原教程图示：Coding the player — build_dotnet.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/build_dotnet.webp)

![原教程图示：Coding the player — export_variable.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/export_variable.webp)

Your `player.gd` script should already contain
a `_ready()` and a `_process()` function.
If you didn't select the default template shown above,
create these functions while following the lesson.

The `_ready()` function is called when a node enters the scene tree, which is
a good time to find the size of the game window:

```gdscript
func _ready():
    screen_size = get_viewport_rect().size
```

```csharp
public override void _Ready()
{
    ScreenSize = GetViewportRect().Size;
}
```

Now we can use the `_process()` function to define what the player will do.
`_process()` is called every frame, so we'll use it to update elements of our
game, which we expect will change often. For the player, we need to do the
following:

- Check for input.
- Move in the given direction.
- Play the appropriate animation.

First, we need to check for input - is the player pressing a key? For this game,
we have 4 direction inputs to check. Input actions are defined in the Project
Settings under "Input Map". Here, you can define custom events and assign
different keys, mouse events, or other inputs to them. For this game, we will
map the arrow keys to the four directions.

title: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
heading: Coding the player
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Click on *Project -> Project Settings* to open the project settings window and
click on the *Input Map* tab at the top. Type "move_right" in the top bar and
click the "Add" button to add the `move_right` action.

![原教程图示：Coding the player — input-mapping-add-action.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/input-mapping-add-action.webp)

We need to assign a key to this action. Click the "+" icon on the right, to
open the event manager window.

![原教程图示：Coding the player — input-mapping-add-key.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/input-mapping-add-key.webp)

The "Listening for Input..." field should automatically be selected.
Press the "right" key on your keyboard, and the menu should look like this now.

![原教程图示：Coding the player — input-mapping-event-configuration.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/input-mapping-event-configuration.webp)

Select the "ok" button. The "right" key is now associated with the `move_right` action.

Repeat these steps to add three more mappings:

1. `move_left` mapped to the left arrow key.
2. `move_up` mapped to the up arrow key.
3. And `move_down` mapped to the down arrow key.

Your input map tab should look like this:

![原教程图示：Coding the player — input-mapping-completed.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/input-mapping-completed.webp)

Click the "Close" button to close the project settings.

Note

We only mapped one key to each input action, but you can map multiple keys,
joystick buttons, or mouse buttons to the same input action.

You can detect whether a key is pressed using `Input.is_action_pressed()`,
which returns `true` if it's pressed or `false` if it isn't.

```gdscript
func _process(delta):
    var velocity = Vector2.ZERO # The player's movement vector.
    if Input.is_action_pressed("move_right"):
        velocity.x += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("move_left"):
        velocity.x -= 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("move_down"):
        velocity.y += 1
    if Input.is_action_pressed("move_up"):
        velocity.y -= 1

    if velocity.length() > 0:
        velocity = velocity.normalized() * speed
        $AnimatedSprite2D.play()
    else:
        $AnimatedSprite2D.stop()
```

title: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
heading: Coding the player
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community

title: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
heading: Coding the player
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Now that we have a movement direction, we can update the player's position. We
can also use `clamp()` to prevent it from leaving the screen. *Clamping* a
value means restricting it to a given range. Add the following to the bottom of
the `_process` function (make sure it's not indented under the else):

```gdscript
position += velocity * delta
position = position.clamp(Vector2.ZERO, screen_size)
```

```csharp
Position += velocity * (float)delta;
Position = new Vector2(
    x: Mathf.Clamp(Position.X, 0, ScreenSize.X),
    y: Mathf.Clamp(Position.Y, 0, ScreenSize.Y)
);
```

Tip

The delta parameter in the _process() function refers to the *frame
length* - the amount of time that the previous frame took to complete.
Using this value ensures that your movement will remain consistent even
if the frame rate changes.

Click "Run Current Scene" (`F6`, `Cmd + R` on macOS) and confirm you can move
the player around the screen in all directions.

Warning

If you get an error in the "Debugger" panel that says

`Attempt to call function 'play' in base 'null instance' on a null
instance`

this likely means you spelled the name of the AnimatedSprite2D node
wrong. Node names are case-sensitive and `$NodeName` must match
the name you see in the scene tree.

#### Choosing animations

Now that the player can move, we need to change which animation the
AnimatedSprite2D is playing based on its direction. We have the "walk" animation,
which shows the player walking to the right. This animation should be flipped
horizontally using the `flip_h` property for left movement. We also have the
"up" animation, which should be flipped vertically with `flip_v` for downward
movement. Let's place this code at the end of the `_process()` function:

```gdscript
if velocity.x != 0:
    $AnimatedSprite2D.animation = "walk"
    $AnimatedSprite2D.flip_v = false
    # See the note below about the following boolean assignment.
    $AnimatedSprite2D.flip_h = velocity.x < 0
elif velocity.y != 0:
    $AnimatedSprite2D.animation = "up"
    $AnimatedSprite2D.flip_v = velocity.y > 0
```

title: 完整二维小游戏：移动、动画切换与受击
heading: Preparing for collisions
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
This defines a custom signal called "hit" that we will have our player emit
(send out) when it collides with an enemy. We will use `Area2D` to detect the
collision. Select the `Player` node and click the "Node" tab next to the
Inspector tab to see the list of signals the player can emit:

![原教程图示：Preparing for collisions — player_signals.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/player_signals.webp)

Notice our custom "hit" signal is there as well! Since our enemies are going to
be `RigidBody2D` nodes, we want the `body_entered(body: Node2D)` signal. This
signal will be emitted when a body contacts the player. Click "Connect.." and
the "Connect a Signal" window appears.

Godot will create a function with that exact name directly in script
for you. You don't need to change the default settings right now.

Warning

If you're using an external text editor (for example, Visual Studio Code),
a bug currently prevents Godot from doing so. You'll be sent to your external
editor, but the new function won't be there.

In this case, you'll need to write the function yourself into the Player's
script file.

![原教程图示：Preparing for collisions — player_signal_connection.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-007/player_signal_connection.webp)

Note the green icon indicating that a signal is connected to this function; this does
not mean the function exists, only that the signal will attempt to connect to a function
with that name, so double-check that the spelling of the function matches exactly!

Next, add this code to the function:

```gdscript
func _on_body_entered(_body):
    hide() # Player disappears after being hit.
    hit.emit()
    # Must be deferred as we can't change physics properties on a physics callback.
    $CollisionShape2D.set_deferred("disabled", true)
```

title: 完整二维小游戏：敌人场景与离屏清理
heading: 完整二维小游戏：敌人场景与离屏清理
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 完整二维小游戏：敌人场景与离屏清理

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

为敌人建立可生成的独立场景，配置动画和离开画面后的释放逻辑。

## 前提

- DEV-006
- 基础 GDScript

## 中文操作路线

1. 建立 RigidBody2D 敌人根节点，并按原文设置碰撞与重力相关参数。
2. 添加动画精灵、碰撞形状和可见性通知节点，检查它们的相对位置。
3. 在初始化时从可用动画中选择外观，使同一场景能生成不同敌人。
4. 连接离开屏幕的信号，调用 queue_free 释放敌人实例。
5. 保存为独立场景，交给下一章主场景负责生成。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

记录一分钟内活动敌人数量；让敌人出屏后确认数量回落，而不是持续累积。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 敌人不会因默认重力朝错误方向下坠。
- [ ] 动画名称来自当前 SpriteFrames。
- [ ] 出屏实例会释放，场景树没有无界增长。

## 版本与边界

这是穿越屏幕的敌人示例，不包含寻路或追踪 AI。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Creating the enemy

Now it's time to make the enemies our player will have to dodge. Their behavior
will not be very complex: mobs will spawn randomly at the edges of the screen,
choose a random direction, and move in a straight line.

We'll create a `Mob` scene, which we can then *instance* to create any number
of independent mobs in the game.

#### Node setup

Click Scene -> New Scene from the top menu and add the following nodes:

- [RigidBody2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_rigidbody2d.html#class-rigidbody2d) (named `Mob`)

  > - [AnimatedSprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animatedsprite2d.html#class-animatedsprite2d)
  > - [CollisionShape2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_collisionshape2d.html#class-collisionshape2d)
  > - [VisibleOnScreenNotifier2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_visibleonscreennotifier2d.html#class-visibleonscreennotifier2d)

Don't forget to set the children so they can't be selected, like you did with
the Player scene. This is done by selecting the parent node (`RigidBody2D`) in the
Scene tree dock, then using the Group button at the top of the 2D editor
(or pressing `Ctrl + G`).

title: 完整二维小游戏：敌人场景与离屏清理
heading: Node setup
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Select the `Mob` node and set its `Gravity Scale`
property in the [RigidBody2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_rigidbody2d.html#class-rigidbody2d)
section of the inspector to `0`.
This will prevent the mob from falling downwards.

In addition, under the [CollisionObject2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_collisionobject2d.html#class-collisionobject2d)
section just beneath the **RigidBody2D** section,
expand the **Collision** group and
uncheck the `1` inside the `Mask` property.
This will ensure the mobs do not collide with each other.

![原教程图示：Node setup — set_collision_mask.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-008/set_collision_mask.webp)

Set up the [AnimatedSprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animatedsprite2d.html#class-animatedsprite2d) like you did for the
player. This time, we have 3 animations: `fly`, `swim`, and `walk`. There
are two images for each animation in the art folder.

The `Animation Speed` property has to be set for each individual animation. Adjust it to `3` for all 3 animations.

![原教程图示：Node setup — mob_animations.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-008/mob_animations.webp)

You can use the "Play Animation" buttons on the right of the `Animation Speed` input field to preview your animations.

We'll select one of these animations randomly so that the mobs will have some
variety.

Like the player images, these mob images need to be scaled down. Set the
`AnimatedSprite2D`'s `Scale` property to `(0.75, 0.75)`.

As in the `Player` scene, add a `CapsuleShape2D` for the collision. To align
the shape with the image, you'll need to set the `Rotation` property
to `90` (under "Transform" in the Inspector).

Save the scene.

#### Enemy script

Add a script to the `Mob` like this:

```gdscript
extends RigidBody2D
```

```csharp
using Godot;

public partial class Mob : RigidBody2D
{
    // Don't forget to rebuild the project.
}
```

Now let's look at the rest of the script. In `_ready()` we play the animation
and randomly choose one of the three animation types:

title: 完整二维小游戏：生成、计分与回合循环
heading: 完整二维小游戏：生成、计分与回合循环
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 完整二维小游戏：生成、计分与回合循环

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

把玩家、敌人、计时器和边界路径组合成完整一局游戏。

## 前提

- DEV-007
- DEV-008

## 中文操作路线

1. 建立主场景，添加玩家实例、开始位置、计时器及用于生成敌人的路径。
2. 用 Path2D 定义生成边界，再用 PathFollow2D 选择边界上的生成位置。
3. 加载敌人 PackedScene，每次计时器触发时实例化并赋予位置与速度。
4. 实现 new_game 与 game_over，分别重置分数和启动或停止相关计时器。
5. 独立测试主场景后，把它设为项目入口，再接入 HUD。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

把敌人生成间隔改为三个档位，测量每局开始到首个敌人出现的延迟，并验证结束后不再生成。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 敌人从预期边缘进入画面。
- [ ] 开始新局时分数归零。
- [ ] 游戏结束停止生成和计分计时器。

## 版本与边界

随机性只负责生成位置、方向或速度的变化；不应据此推断游戏一定具有更强留存。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### The main game scene

Now it's time to bring everything we did together into a playable game scene.

Create a new scene and add a [Node](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_node.html#class-node) named `Main`.
(The reason we are using Node instead of Node2D is because this node will
be a container for handling game logic. It does not require 2D functionality itself.)

Click the **Instance** button (represented by a chain link icon) and select your saved
`player.tscn`.

![原教程图示：The main game scene — instance_scene.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-009/instance_scene.webp)

Now, add the following nodes as children of `Main`, and name them as shown:

- [Timer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_timer.html#class-timer) (named `MobTimer`) - to control how often mobs
  spawn
- [Timer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_timer.html#class-timer) (named `ScoreTimer`) - to increment the score
  every second
- [Timer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_timer.html#class-timer) (named `StartTimer`) - to give a delay before
  starting
- [Marker2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_marker2d.html#class-marker2d) (named `StartPosition`) - to indicate
  the player's start position

Set the `Wait Time` property of each of the `Timer` nodes as follows (values are in seconds):

- `MobTimer`: `0.5`
- `ScoreTimer`: `1`
- `StartTimer`: `2`

title: 完整二维小游戏：生成、计分与回合循环
heading: The main game scene
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
In addition, set the `One Shot` property of `StartTimer` to "On" and set
`Position` of the `StartPosition` node to `(240, 450)`.

#### Spawning mobs

The Main node will be spawning new mobs, and we want them to appear at a random
location on the edge of the screen. Click the `Main` node in the Scene dock, then
add a child [Path2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_path2d.html#class-path2d) node named `MobPath`. When you select
`Path2D`, you will see some new buttons at the top of the editor:

![原教程图示：Spawning mobs — path2d_buttons.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-009/path2d_buttons.webp)

Select the middle one ("Add Point") and draw the path by clicking to add the
points at the corners shown. To have the points snap to the grid, make sure "Use
Grid Snap" and "Use Smart Snap" are both selected. These options can be found to the
left of the "Lock" button, appearing as a magnet next to some dots and
intersecting lines, respectively.

![原教程图示：Spawning mobs — grid_snap_button.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-009/grid_snap_button.webp)

Important

Draw the path in *clockwise* order, or your mobs will spawn
pointing *outwards* instead of *inwards*!

![原教程图示：Spawning mobs — draw_path2d.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-009/draw_path2d.gif)

After placing point `4` in the image, click the "Close Curve" button and your
curve will be complete.

Now that the path is defined, add a [PathFollow2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_pathfollow2d.html#class-pathfollow2d)
node as a child of `MobPath` and name it `MobSpawnLocation`. This node will
automatically rotate and follow the path as it moves, so we can use it to select
a random position and direction along the path.

Your scene should look like this:

![原教程图示：Spawning mobs — main_scene_nodes.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-009/main_scene_nodes.webp)

#### Main script

Add a script to `Main`. At the top of the script, we use
`@export var mob_scene: PackedScene` to allow us to choose the Mob scene we want
to instance.

```gdscript
extends Node

@export var mob_scene: PackedScene
var score
```

title: 完整二维小游戏：生成、计分与回合循环
heading: Main script
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community

heading: Testing the scene
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
#### Testing the scene

Let's test the scene to make sure everything is working. Add this `new_game`
call to `_ready()`:

```gdscript
func _ready():
    new_game()
```

```csharp
public override void _Ready()
{
    NewGame();
}
```

Let's also assign `Main` as our "Main Scene" - the one that runs automatically
when the game launches. Press the "Play" button and select `main.tscn` when
prompted.

Tip

If you had already set another scene as the "Main Scene", you can right
click `main.tscn` in the FileSystem dock and select "Set As Main Scene".

You should be able to move the player around, see mobs spawning, and see the
player disappear when hit by a mob.

When you're sure everything is working, remove the call to `new_game()` from
`_ready()` and replace it with `pass`.

What's our game lacking? Some user interface. In the next lesson, we'll add a
title screen and display the player's score.

---

title: 完整二维小游戏：HUD、开始按钮与重开
heading: 完整二维小游戏：HUD、开始按钮与重开
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 完整二维小游戏：HUD、开始按钮与重开

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

让分数、提示和开始按钮独立于游戏世界，连接开局、结束与清理流程。

## 前提

- DEV-009
- DEV-004

## 中文操作路线

1. 以 CanvasLayer 建立 HUD，添加分数标签、提示标签、开始按钮和消息计时器。
2. 设置控件锚点与布局，使不同窗口尺寸下仍处于预期位置。
3. 把按钮点击转换成 start_game 信号，让主场景响应新局请求。
4. 实现分数更新、短时提示和游戏结束提示，按顺序隐藏与显示按钮。
5. 新局开始前清理旧敌人，避免上一局实例留在场景中。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

连续输掉并重开三局，记录分数、按钮、消息和旧敌人的状态是否全部复位。

## 验收清单

- [ ] HUD 不随世界物体运动而漂移。
- [ ] 同一局只触发一次开始事件。
- [ ] 重开后没有旧敌人或上局分数残留。

## 版本与边界

HUD示例是结构练习。实际沉浸式像素游戏可减少屏幕控件数量，但不能省略必要状态反馈。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Heads up display

The final piece our game needs is a User Interface (UI) to display things like
score, a "game over" message, and a restart button.

Create a new scene, click the "Other Node" button and add a [CanvasLayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvaslayer.html#class-canvaslayer) node named
`HUD`. "HUD" stands for "heads-up display", an informational display that
appears as an overlay on top of the game view.

The [CanvasLayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvaslayer.html#class-canvaslayer) node lets us draw our UI elements on
a layer above the rest of the game, so that the information it displays isn't
covered up by any game elements like the player or mobs.

The HUD needs to display the following information:

- Score, changed by `ScoreTimer`.
- A message, such as "Game Over" or "Get Ready!"
- A "Start" button to begin the game.

The basic node for UI elements is [Control](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_control.html#class-control). To create our
UI, we'll use two types of [Control](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_control.html#class-control) nodes: [Label](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_label.html#class-label) and [Button](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_button.html#class-button).

Create the following as children of the `HUD` node:

title: 完整二维小游戏：HUD、开始按钮与重开
heading: Heads up display
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
- [Label](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_label.html#class-label) named `ScoreLabel`.
- [Label](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_label.html#class-label) named `Message`.
- [Button](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_button.html#class-button) named `StartButton`.
- [Timer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_timer.html#class-timer) named `MessageTimer`.

Click on the `ScoreLabel` and type a number into the `Text` field in the
Inspector. The default font for `Control` nodes is small and doesn't scale
well. There is a font file included in the game assets called
"Xolonium-Regular.ttf". To use this font, do the following:

Under "Theme Overrides > Fonts", choose "Load" and select the "Xolonium-Regular.ttf" file.

![原教程图示：Heads up display — custom_font_load_font.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-010/custom_font_load_font.webp)

The font size is still too small, increase it to `64` under "Theme Overrides > Font Sizes".
Once you've done this with the `ScoreLabel`, repeat the changes for the `Message` and `StartButton` nodes.

![原教程图示：Heads up display — custom_font_size.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-010/custom_font_size.webp)

Note

**Anchors:** `Control` nodes have a position and size,
but they also have anchors. Anchors define the origin -
the reference point for the edges of the node.

Arrange the nodes as shown below.
You can drag the nodes to place them manually, or for more precise placement,
use "Anchor Presets".

![原教程图示：Heads up display — ui_anchor.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-010/ui_anchor.webp)

#### ScoreLabel

1. Add the text `0`.
2. Set the "Horizontal Alignment" and "Vertical Alignment" to `Center`.
3. Choose the "Anchor Preset" `Center Top`.

#### Message

1. Add the text `Dodge the Creeps!`.
2. Set the "Horizontal Alignment" and "Vertical Alignment" to `Center`.
3. Set the "Autowrap Mode" to `Word`, otherwise the label will stay on one line.
4. Under "Control - Layout/Transform" set "Size X" to `480` to use the entire width of the screen.
5. Choose the "Anchor Preset" `Center`.

#### StartButton

heading: Connecting HUD to Main
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
```csharp
var hud = GetNode<HUD>("HUD");
hud.UpdateScore(_score);
hud.ShowMessage("Get Ready!");
```

In `game_over()` we need to call the corresponding `HUD` function:

```gdscript
$HUD.show_game_over()
```

```csharp
GetNode<HUD>("HUD").ShowGameOver();
```

Finally, add this to `_on_score_timer_timeout()` to keep the display in sync
with the changing score:

```gdscript
$HUD.update_score(score)
```

```csharp
GetNode<HUD>("HUD").UpdateScore(_score);
```

Warning

Remember to remove the call to `new_game()` from
`_ready()` if you haven't already, otherwise
your game will start automatically.

Now you're ready to play! Click the "Play the Project" button.

#### Removing old creeps

If you play until "Game Over" and then start a new game right away, the creeps
from the previous game may still be on the screen. It would be better if they
all disappeared at the start of a new game. We just need a way to tell *all* the
mobs to remove themselves. We can do this with the "group" feature.

In the `Mob` scene, select the root node and click the "Node" tab next to the
Inspector (the same place where you find the node's signals). Next to "Signals",
click "Groups" to open the group overview
and the "+" button to open the "Create New Group" dialog.

![原教程图示：Removing old creeps — group_tab.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-010/group_tab.webp)

Name the group `mobs` and click "ok" to add a new scene group.

![原教程图示：Removing old creeps — add_group_dialog.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-010/add_group_dialog.webp)

Now all mobs will be in the "mobs" group.

![原教程图示：Removing old creeps — scene_group_mobs.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-010/scene_group_mobs.webp)

We can then add the following line to the `new_game()` function in `Main`:

```gdscript
get_tree().call_group("mobs", "queue_free")
```

```csharp
// Note that for calling Godot-provided methods with strings,
// we have to use the original Godot snake_case name.
GetTree().CallGroup("mobs", Node.MethodName.QueueFree);
```

The `call_group()` function calls the named function on every node in a
group - in this case we are telling every mob to delete itself.

a bit by adding a background, looping music, and some keyboard shortcuts.
