title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

建立可管理的动作状态转换，理解混合树、状态机与动画播放控制的职责。

## 前提

- 已使用 AnimationPlayer 创建动画
- DEV-013

## 中文操作路线

1. 先准备可独立播放的 AnimationPlayer 动画，再创建引用它的 AnimationTree。
2. 阅读不同根节点类型，按需求选择混合树或状态机。
3. 为 idle、walk、attack 建立状态与转换，并指定必要的条件和切换模式。
4. 通过 AnimationTree 参数和状态机 playback 控制运行，避免同时用多套播放入口竞争。
5. 检查共享轨道的默认值与 RESET 动画等混合要求，防止状态切换后残留属性。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

制作 idle→walk→attack→idle 的最小流程，禁止攻击未结束时被普通移动状态立即打断。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 状态转换条件可从代码和图中清晰追溯。
- [ ] 切换动作后位置、透明度等属性不会残留。
- [ ] 静止与移动之间没有错误循环或不可达状态。

## 版本与边界

官方页面也涵盖3D、骨骼和高级混合。逐帧像素动画并不一定需要插值混合；优先选能保持帧形状清晰的切换方式。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Using AnimationTree

#### Introduction

With [AnimationPlayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animationplayer.html#class-animationplayer), Godot has one of the most flexible animation systems that you can find in any game engine.
It is pretty much unique in its ability to animate almost any property in any node or resource, and its dedicated transform, bezier,
function calling, audio, and sub-animation tracks.

However, the support for blending those animations via `AnimationPlayer` is limited, as you can only set a fixed cross-fade transition time.

[AnimationTree](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animationtree.html#class-animationtree) is a new node introduced in Godot 3.1 to deal with advanced transitions.
It replaces the ancient `AnimationTreePlayer`, while adding a huge amount of features and flexibility.

#### AnimationTree and AnimationPlayer

Before starting, know that an `AnimationTree` node does not contain its own animations.
Instead, it uses animations contained in an `AnimationPlayer` node. You create, edit, or import your animations in an `AnimationPlayer`
and then use an `AnimationTree` to control the playback.

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: AnimationTree and AnimationPlayer
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
`AnimationPlayer` and `AnimationTree` can be used in both 2D and 3D scenes. When importing 3D scenes and their animations, you can use
[name suffixes](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/assets_pipeline/importing_3d_scenes/node_type_customization.html#animation-loop-loop-cycle)
to simplify the process and import with the correct properties. At the end, the imported Godot scene will contain the animations in an `AnimationPlayer` node.
Since you rarely use imported scenes directly in Godot (they are either instantiated or inherited from), you can place the `AnimationTree` node in your
new scene which contains the imported one. Afterwards, point the `AnimationTree` node to the `AnimationPlayer` that was created in the imported scene.

This is how it's done in the [Third Person Shooter demo](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/678), for reference:

![原教程图示：AnimationTree and AnimationPlayer — animtree_treeandplayersetup.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_treeandplayersetup.png)

A new scene was created for the player with a `CharacterBody3D` as root. Inside this scene, the original `.dae` (Collada) file was instantiated
and an `AnimationTree` node was created.

#### Creating a tree

To use an `AnimationTree`, you have to set a root node. An animation root node is a class that contains and evaluates sub-nodes and outputs an animation.
There are 3 types of sub-nodes:

1. Animation nodes, which reference an animation from the linked `AnimationPlayer`.
2. Animation Root nodes, which are used to blend sub-nodes and can be nested.
3. Animation Blend nodes, which are used in an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`, a 2D graph of nodes. Blend nodes take multiple input ports and give one output port.

A few types of root nodes are available:

![原教程图示：Creating a tree — animtree_rootnodes.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_rootnodes.png)

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: Creating a tree
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
- `AnimationNodeAnimation`: Selects an animation from the list and plays it. This is the simplest root node, and generally not used as a root.
- `AnimationNodeBlendTree`: Contains multiple nodes as children in a graph. Many blend nodes are available, such as mix, blend2, blend3, one shot, etc.
- `AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D`: Allows linear blending between two animation nodes. Control the blend position in a 1D blend space to mix between animations.
- `AnimationNodeBlendSpace2D`: Allows linear blending between three animation nodes. Control the blend position in a 2D blend space to mix between animations.
- `AnimationNodeStateMachine`: Contains multiple nodes as children in a graph. Each node is used as a state, with multiple functions used to alternate between states.

#### Blend tree

When you make an `AnimationNodeBlendTree`, you get an empty 2d graph in the bottom panel, under the AnimationTree tab. It contains only an `Output`
node by default.

![原教程图示：Blend tree — animtree_emptyblendtree.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_emptyblendtree.webp)

In order for animations to play, a node has to be connected to the output. You can add nodes from the **Add Node..** menu or by right clicking an empty space:

![原教程图示：Blend tree — animtree_blendnodes.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_blendnodes.webp)

The simplest connection to make is to connect an `Animation` node to the output directly, which will just play back the animation.

![原教程图示：Blend tree — animtree_animtooutput.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_animtooutput.png)

Following is a description of the other available nodes:

##### Blend2 / Blend3

These nodes will blend between two or three inputs by a user-specified blend value:

![原教程图示：Blend2 / Blend3 — animtree_blend2.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_blend2.gif)

Blending can use **filters** to control individually which tracks get blended and which do not. This can be useful for layering animations on top of each other.

![原教程图示：Blend2 / Blend3 — animtree_filtering.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_filtering.png)

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: Blend2 / Blend3
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
For more complex blending, it is recommended to use blend spaces instead.

##### OneShot

This node will execute an animation once and return when it finishes. You can customize blend times for fading in and out, as well as filters.

![原教程图示：OneShot — animtree_oneshot.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_oneshot.gif)

```gdscript
# Play child animation connected to "shot" port.
animation_tree.set("parameters/OneShot/request", AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FIRE)
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/OneShot/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_FIRE

# Abort child animation connected to "shot" port.
animation_tree.set("parameters/OneShot/request", AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_ABORT)
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/OneShot/request"] = AnimationNodeOneShot.ONE_SHOT_REQUEST_ABORT

# Get current state (read-only).
animation_tree.get("parameters/OneShot/active"))
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/OneShot/active"]
```

```csharp
// Play child animation connected to "shot" port.
animationTree.Set("parameters/OneShot/request", (int)AnimationNodeOneShot.OneShotRequest.Fire);

// Abort child animation connected to "shot" port.
animationTree.Set("parameters/OneShot/request", (int)AnimationNodeOneShot.OneShotRequest.Abort);

// Get current state (read-only).
animationTree.Get("parameters/OneShot/active");
```

##### TimeSeek

This node allows you to seek to a time in the animation connected to its in input. Use this node to play an `Animation` starting from a certain playback position.
Note that the seek request value is measured in seconds, so if you would like to play an animation from the beginning, set the value to `0.0`, or if you would like
to play an animation from 3 seconds in, set the value to `3.0`.

![原教程图示：TimeSeek — animtree_timeseek.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_timeseek.webp)

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: TimeSeek
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
```gdscript
# Play child animation from the start.
animation_tree.set("parameters/TimeSeek/seek_request", 0.0)
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/TimeSeek/seek_request"] = 0.0

# Play child animation from 12 second timestamp.
animation_tree.set("parameters/TimeSeek/seek_request", 12.0)
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/TimeSeek/seek_request"] = 12.0
```

```csharp
// Play child animation from the start.
animationTree.Set("parameters/TimeSeek/seek_request", 0.0);

// Play child animation from 12 second timestamp.
animationTree.Set("parameters/TimeSeek/seek_request", 12.0);
```

##### TimeScale

This node allows you to scale the speed of the animation connected to its in input. The speed of the animation will be multiplied by the number in the scale
parameter. Setting the scale to 0 will pause the animation. Setting the scale to a negative number will play the animation backwards.

![原教程图示：TimeScale — animtree_timescale.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_timescale.webp)

##### Transition

This node is a simplified version of a StateMachine. You connect animations to the inputs, and the current state index determines which animation to play.
You may specify a crossfade transition time. In the Inspector, you may change the number of input ports, rearrange inputs, or delete inputs.

![原教程图示：Transition — animtree_transition.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_transition.webp)

```gdscript
# Play child animation connected to "state_2" port.
animation_tree.set("parameters/Transition/transition_request", "state_2")
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/Transition/transition_request"] = "state_2"

# Get current state name (read-only).
animation_tree.get("parameters/Transition/current_state")
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/Transition/current_state"]

# Get current state index (read-only).
animation_tree.get("parameters/Transition/current_index"))
# Alternative syntax (same result).
animation_tree["parameters/Transition/current_index"]
```

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: Transition
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
```csharp
// Play child animation connected to "state_2" port.
animationTree.Set("parameters/Transition/transition_request", "state_2");

// Get current state name (read-only).
animationTree.Get("parameters/Transition/current_state");

// Get current state index (read-only).
animationTree.Get("parameters/Transition/current_index");
```

##### StateMachine

When you make an `AnimationNodeStateMachine`, you get an empty 2d graph in the bottom panel, under the AnimationTree tab. It contains a `Start` and `End`
state by default.

![原教程图示：StateMachine — animtree_emptystatemachine.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_emptystatemachine.webp)

To add states, right click or use the **create new nodes** button, whose icon is a plus in a box. You can add animations, blendspaces, blendtrees, or even
another StateMachine. To edit one of these more complex sub-nodes, click on the pencil icon on the right of the state. To return to the original StateMachine,
click **Root** on the top left of the panel.

Before the StateMachine can do anything useful, the states must be connected with transitions. To add a transition, click the **connect nodes** button, which is
a line with a right-facing arrow, and drag between two states. You can create 2 transitions between states, one going in each direction.

![原教程图示：StateMachine — animtree_connections.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_connections.gif)

There are 3 types of transitions:

![原教程图示：StateMachine — animtree_transitiontypes.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_transitiontypes.png)

- *Immediate*: Will switch to the next state immediately.
- *Sync*: Will switch to the next state immediately, but will seek the new state to the playback position of the old state.
- *At End*: Will wait for the current state playback to end, then switch to the beginning of the next state animation.

Transitions also have a few properties. Click a transition and it will be displayed in the inspector:

![原教程图示：StateMachine — animtree_statemachinetransitionproperties.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_statemachinetransitionproperties.webp)

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: StateMachine
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
- *Xfade Time* is the time to cross-fade between this state and the next.
- *Xfade Curve* is a cross-fade following a curve rather than a linear blend.
- *Reset* determines whether the state you are switching into plays from the beginning (true) or not (false).
- *Priority* is used together with the `travel()` function from code (more on this later). Lower priority transitions are preferred when travelling through the tree.
- *Switch Mode* is the transition type (see above). It can be changed after creation here.
- *Advance Mode* determines the advance mode. If `Disabled`, the transition will not be used. If `Enabled`, the transition will only be used during `travel()`. If `Auto`, the transition will be used if the advance condition and expression are true, or if there are no advance conditions/expressions.

###### Advance Condition and Advance Expression

The last 2 properties in a StateMachine transition are `Advance Condition` and `Advance Expression.` When the Advance Mode is set to *Auto*, these
determine if the transition will advance or not.

Advance Condition is a true/false check. You may put a custom variable name in the text field, and when the StateMachine reaches this transition,
it will check if your variable is *true*. If so, the transition continues. Note that the advance condition **only** checks if a variable is *true*,
and it cannot check for falseness.

This gives the Advance Condition a very limited capability. If you wanted to make a transition back and forth based on one property, you would need to make
2 variables that have opposite values, and check if either of them are true. This is why, in Godot 4, the Advance Expression was added.

The Advance Expression works similar to the Advance Condition, but instead of checking if one variable is true, it evaluates any expression. An expression
is anything you could put in an `if` statement. These are all examples of expressions that would work in the Advance Expression:

- `is_walking`
- `is_walking` == true
- `is_walking && !is_idle`
- `velocity > 0`
- `player.is_on_floor()`

Here is an example of an improperly-set-up StateMachine transition using Advance Condition:

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: Advance Condition and Advance Expression
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_badanimcondition.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_badanimcondition.webp)
![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_badanimcondition.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_badanimcondition.gif)

This is not working because there is a `!` variable in the Advance Condition, which cannot be checked.

Here is the same example, set up properly, using two opposite variables:

![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_goodanimcondition.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_goodanimcondition.webp)
![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_goodanimcondition.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_goodanimcondition.gif)

Here is the same example, but using Advance Expression rather than Advance Condition, which eliminates the need for two variables:

![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_goodanimexpression.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_goodanimexpression.webp)
![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_goodanimexpression2.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_goodanimexpression2.webp)
![原教程图示：Advance Condition and Advance Expression — animtree_goodanimexpression.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_goodanimexpression.gif)

In order to use Advance Expressions, the Advance Expression Base Node has to be set from the Inspector of the AnimationTree node. By default, it is set
to the AnimationTree node itself, but it needs to point to whatever node contains the script with your animation variables.

###### StateMachine travel

One of the nice features in Godot's `StateMachine` implementation is the ability to travel. You can instruct the graph to go from the
current state to another one, while visiting all the intermediate ones. This is done via the A\* algorithm.
If there is no path of transitions starting at the current state and finishing at the destination state, the graph teleports to the destination state.

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: StateMachine travel
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
To use the travel ability, you should first retrieve the [AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animationnodestatemachineplayback.html#class-animationnodestatemachineplayback)
object from the `AnimationTree` node (it is exported as a property), and then call one of its many functions:

```gdscript
var state_machine = animation_tree["parameters/playback"]
state_machine.travel("SomeState")
```

```csharp
AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback stateMachine = (AnimationNodeStateMachinePlayback)animationTree.Get("parameters/playback");
stateMachine.Travel("SomeState");
```

The StateMachine must be running before you can travel. Make sure to either call `start()` or connect a node to **Start**.

#### BlendSpace2D and BlendSpace1D

`BlendSpace2D` is a node to do advanced blending in two dimensions. Points representing animations are added to a 2D space and then a position between them
is controlled to determine the blending:

![原教程图示：BlendSpace2D and BlendSpace1D — animtree_blendspace2d.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_blendspace2d.gif)

You may place these points anywhere on the graph by right clicking or using the **add point** button, whose icon is a pen and point.
Wherever you place the points, the triangle between them will be generated automatically using Delaunay.
You may also control and label the ranges in X and Y.

![原教程图示：BlendSpace2D and BlendSpace1D — animtree_blendspacepoints.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_blendspacepoints.gif)

Finally, you may also change the blend mode. By default, blending happens by interpolating points inside the closest triangle. When dealing with 2D
animations (frame by frame), you may want to switch to *Discrete* mode. Alternatively, if you want to keep the current play position when switching
between discrete animations, there is a *Carry* mode. This mode can be changed in the *Blend* menu:

![原教程图示：BlendSpace2D and BlendSpace1D — animtree_blendmode.png](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_blendmode.png)

BlendSpace1D works just like BlendSpace2D, but in one dimension (a line). Triangles are not used.

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: BlendSpace2D and BlendSpace1D
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：BlendSpace2D and BlendSpace1D — animtree_blendspace1d.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_blendspace1d.webp)

#### For better blending

In Godot 4.0+, in order for the blending results to be deterministic (reproducible and always consistent),
the blended property values must have a specific initial value.
For example, in the case of two animations to be blended, if one animation has a property track and the other does not,
the blended animation is calculated as if the latter animation had a property track with the initial value.

When using Position/Rotation/Scale 3D tracks for Skeleton3D bones, the initial value is Bone Rest.
For other properties, the initial value is `0` and if the track is present in the `RESET` animation,
the value of its first keyframe is used instead.

For example, the following AnimationPlayer has two animations, but one of them lacks a Property track for Position.

![原教程图示：For better blending — blending1.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/blending1.webp)

This means that the animation lacking that will treat those Positions as `Vector2(0, 0)`.

![原教程图示：For better blending — blending2.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/blending2.webp)

This problem can be solved by adding a Property track for Position as an initial value to the `RESET` animation.

![原教程图示：For better blending — blending3.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/blending3.webp)
![原教程图示：For better blending — blending4.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/blending4.webp)

Note

Be aware that the `RESET` animation exists to define the default pose when loading an object originally.
It is assumed to have only one frame and is not expected to be played back using the timeline.

Also keep in mind that the Rotation 3D tracks and the Property tracks for 2D rotation
with Interpolation Type set to Linear Angle or Cubic Angle will prevent rotations greater than 180 degrees
from the initial value as blended animation.

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: For better blending
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
This can be useful for Skeleton3Ds to prevent the bones penetrating the body when blending animations.
Therefore, Skeleton3D's Bone Rest values should be as close to the midpoint of the movable range as possible.
**This means that for humanoid models, it is preferable to import them in a T-pose**.

![原教程图示：For better blending — blending5.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/blending5.webp)

You can see that the shortest rotation path from Bone Rests is prioritized rather than the shortest rotation path between animations.

If you need to rotate Skeleton3D itself more than 180 degrees by blend animations for movement, you can use Root Motion.

#### Root motion

When working with 3D animations, a popular technique is for animators to use the root skeleton bone to give motion to the rest of the skeleton.
This allows animating characters in a way where steps actually match the floor below. It also allows precise interaction with objects during cinematics.

When playing back the animation in Godot, it is possible to select this bone as the *root motion track*. Doing so will cancel the bone
transformation visually (the animation will stay in place).

![原教程图示：Root motion — animtree_rootmotiontrack.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_rootmotiontrack.webp)

Afterwards, the actual motion can be retrieved via the [AnimationTree](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_animationtree.html#class-animationtree) API as a transform:

```gdscript
# Get the motion delta.
animation_tree.get_root_motion_position()
animation_tree.get_root_motion_rotation()
animation_tree.get_root_motion_scale()

# Get the actual blended value of the animation.
animation_tree.get_root_motion_position_accumulator()
animation_tree.get_root_motion_rotation_accumulator()
animation_tree.get_root_motion_scale_accumulator()
```

```csharp
// Get the motion delta.
animationTree.GetRootMotionPosition();
animationTree.GetRootMotionRotation();
animationTree.GetRootMotionScale();

// Get the actual blended value of the animation.
animationTree.GetRootMotionPositionAccumulator();
animationTree.GetRootMotionRotationAccumulator();
animationTree.GetRootMotionScaleAccumulator();
```

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: Root motion
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
This can be fed to functions such as [CharacterBody3D.move_and_slide](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_characterbody3d.html#class-characterbody3d-method-move-and-slide) to control the character movement.

There is also a tool node, `RootMotionView`, you can place a scene that will act as a custom floor for your
character and animations (this node is disabled by default during the game).

![原教程图示：Root motion — animtree15.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree15.gif)

#### Controlling from code

After building the tree and previewing it, the only question remaining is "How is all this controlled from code?".

Keep in mind that the animation nodes are just resources, so they are shared between all instances using them.
Setting values in the nodes directly will affect all instances of the scene that uses this `AnimationTree`.
This is generally undesirable, but does have some cool use cases, e.g. you can copy and paste parts of your animation tree,
or reuse nodes with a complex layout (such as a StateMachine or blend space) in different animation trees.

The actual animation data is contained in the `AnimationTree` node and is accessed via properties.
Check the "Parameters" section of the `AnimationTree` node to see all the parameters that can be modified in real-time:

![原教程图示：Controlling from code — animtree_parameters.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_parameters.webp)

This is handy because it makes it possible to animate them from an `AnimationPlayer`, or even the `AnimationTree` itself,
allowing very complex animation logic.

To modify these values from code, you must obtain the property path. You can find them by hovering your mouse over any of the parameters:

![原教程图示：Controlling from code — animtree_propertypath.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-023/animtree_propertypath.webp)

Then you can set or read them:

```gdscript
animation_tree.set("parameters/eye_blend/blend_amount", 1.0)
# Alternate syntax (same result)
animation_tree["parameters/eye_blend/blend_amount"] = 1.0
```

```csharp
animationTree.Set("parameters/eye_blend/blend_amount", 1.0);
```

Note

title: AnimationTree：动作混合与状态机
heading: Controlling from code
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Advance Expressions from a StateMachine will not be found under the parameters. This is because they are held in another script rather than the
AnimationTree itself. Advance Conditions will be found under parameters.

---

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

用分层滚动制造深度，检查重复范围和镜头移动时的接缝。

## 前提

- 有适合循环的背景素材
- 理解 Camera2D

## 中文操作路线

1. 建立 Parallax2D 并添加可见背景，先让相机运动验证基础跟随关系。
2. 用 scroll_scale 调整远近层相对相机的移动速度，逐层设置而非同时修改。
3. 配置 repeat_size 等重复参数，使重复范围覆盖正确的纹理尺寸。
4. 检查子节点偏移、缩放与可视窗口尺寸，避免重复时露出空白或错位。
5. 使用正反方向镜头运动与较大窗口测试循环边界。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

为村庄外景制作远山、云层、近景树影三个层，每层采用不同滚动比例并保持无缝循环。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 镜头反向移动时没有突然跳变。
- [ ] 接缝处纹理连续且不会露出空白。
- [ ] 视差不会使可交互前景的位置产生误导。

## 版本与边界

Parallax2D 的用法应按4.5页面操作；旧教程中的 ParallaxBackground/ParallaxLayer 结构不宜直接混用。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### 2D Parallax

#### Introduction

Parallax is an effect used to simulate depth by having textures move at different speeds relative to the camera. Godot
provides the [Parallax2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d) node to achieve this effect. It can still be easy to get tripped
up though, so this page provides in-depth descriptions of some properties and how to fix some common mistakes.

Note

This page covers how to use [Parallax2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d), which is
recommended to use over the [ParallaxLayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallaxlayer.html#class-parallaxlayer) and
[ParallaxBackground](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallaxbackground.html#class-parallaxbackground) nodes.

#### Getting started

The parallax node supports adding nodes that render things as children, so you can use one or many nodes to make up each
layer. To begin, place each node or nodes you want to have scroll independently as a child of their own parallax node.
Make sure that the top left of the textures used are at the `(0, 0)` crossing, like in the image below. See the section
on [positioning](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/2d/2d_parallax.html#doc-2d-parallax-positioning) for why this is important.

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Getting started
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Getting started — 2d_parallax_size_viewport.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_size_viewport.webp)

The scene above uses one prepared texture for the higher clouds in a [Sprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d), but you could
just as easily use multiple nodes spaced out to compose the layer.

#### Scroll scale

The backbone of the parallax effect is the [scroll_scale](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-scroll-scale) property.
It works as a scroll-speed multiplier, allowing layers to move at a different speed than the camera for each axis set.
A value of 1 makes the parallax node scroll at the same speed as the camera. If you want your image to look further away
when scrolling, use a value lower than 1, with 0 bringing it to a complete stop. If you want something to appear closer
to the camera, use a value higher than 1, making it scroll faster.

The scene above is comprised of five layers. Some good [scroll_scale](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-scroll-scale)
values might be:

- `(0.7, 1)` - Forest
- `(0.5, 1)` - Hills
- `(0.3, 1)` - Lower Clouds
- `(0.2, 1)` - Higher Clouds
- `(0.1, 1)` - Sky

The video below displays how these values affect scrolling while in-game:

[A scene with five layers scrolling at different speeds（本地原视频；下方为10%、50%、90%位置静态抽帧，未转录视频内容）](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_scroll_scale.webm)

![A scene with five layers scrolling at different speeds：原视频抽帧 0.96 秒（静态观察，不是视频转录）](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_scroll_scale-keyframe-1.png)

![A scene with five layers scrolling at different speeds：原视频抽帧 4.8 秒（静态观察，不是视频转录）](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_scroll_scale-keyframe-2.png)

![A scene with five layers scrolling at different speeds：原视频抽帧 8.64 秒（静态观察，不是视频转录）](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_scroll_scale-keyframe-3.png)

#### Infinite repeat

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Infinite repeat
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
[Parallax2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d) provides a bonus effect that gives textures the illusion of repeating infinitely.
[repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size) tells the node to snap its position forward or back when the
camera scrolls by the set value. This effect is achieved by adding a single repeat to all the child canvas items offset
by the value. While the camera scrolls between the image and its repeat, it invisibly snaps back giving the appearance
of a looping image.

![原教程图示：Infinite repeat — 2d_parallax_scroll.gif](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_scroll.gif)

Being a delicate effect, it's easy for unfamiliar users to make mistakes with their setup. Let's go over the "how" and
"why" of a few common problems users encounter.

##### Poor sizing

The infinite repeat effect is easiest to work with when you have an image designed to repeat seamlessly and is the same
size or larger than your viewport **before** setting the [repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size). If
you aren't able to obtain assets that are designed for this task, there are some other things you can do to better
prepare your image in regards to size.

Here is an example of a texture that is too small for its viewport:

![原教程图示：Poor sizing — 2d_parallax_size_bad.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_size_bad.webp)

We can see that the viewport size is 500x300 but the texture is 288x208. If we set the
[repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size) to the size of our image, the infinite repeat effect doesn't
scroll properly because the original texture doesn't cover the viewport. If we set the
[repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size) to the size of the viewport, we have a large gap. What can we
do?

###### Make the viewport smaller

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Make the viewport smaller
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
The simplest answer is to make the viewport the same size or smaller than your textures.
In **Project Settings > Display > Window**, change the
[Viewport Width](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-display-window-size-viewport-width)
and [Viewport Height](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-display-window-size-viewport-height)
settings to match your background.

![原教程图示：Getting started — 2d_parallax_size_viewport.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_size_viewport.webp)

###### Scale the Parallax2D

If you're not aiming for a pixel-perfect style, or don't mind a little blurriness, you may opt to scale the textures
larger to fit your screen. Set the [scale](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_node2d.html#class-node2d-property-scale) of the [Parallax2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d),
and all child textures scale with it.

###### Scale the child nodes

Similar to scaling the [Parallax2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d), you can scale your [Sprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d) nodes to
be large enough to cover the screen. Keep in mind that some settings like
[Parallax2D.repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size) and
[Sprite2D.region_rect](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d-property-region-rect) do not take scaling into account, so it's necessary to
adjust these values based on the scale.

![原教程图示：Scale the child nodes — 2d_parallax_size_scale.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_size_scale.webp)

###### Repeat the textures

You can also start off on the right foot by preparing child nodes earlier in the process. If you have a
[Sprite2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d) you'd like to repeat, but is too small, you can do the following to repeat it:

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Repeat the textures
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
- set [texture_repeat](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-texture-repeat) to [CanvasItem.TEXTURE_REPEAT_ENABLED](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-constant-texture-repeat-enabled)
- set [region_enabled](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d-property-region-enabled) to `true`
- set the [region_rect](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_sprite2d.html#class-sprite2d-property-region-rect) to a multiple of the size of your texture large enough to cover the viewport.

Below, you can see that repeating the image twice makes it large enough to cover the screen.

![原教程图示：Repeat the textures — 2d_parallax_size_repeat.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_size_repeat.webp)

##### Poor positioning

It's common to see users mistakenly set all of their textures to be centered at `(0,0)`:

![原教程图示：Poor positioning — 2d_parallax_single_centered.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_single_centered.webp)

This creates problems with the infinite repeat effect and should be avoided. The "infinite repeat canvas" starts at
`(0,0)` and expands down and to the right to the size of the [repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size)
value.

![原教程图示：Poor positioning — 2d_parallax_single_expand.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_single_expand.webp)

If the textures are centered on the `(0,0)` crossing, the infinite repeat canvas is only partly covered, so it
only partly repeats.

###### Would increasing `repeat_times` fix this?

Increasing [repeat_times](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-times) technically *would* work in some scenarios, but
is a brute force solution and not the problem it is designed to solve (we'll go over this in a bit). A better fix is to
understand how the repeat effect works and set up the parallax textures appropriately to begin with.

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Would increasing `repeat_times` fix this?
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
First, check to see if any textures are spilling over onto the negative parts of the canvas. Make sure the textures
used in the parallax nodes fit inside the "infinite repeat canvas" starting at `(0,0)`. That way, if
[Parallax2D.repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size) is set correctly, it should look something like
this, with one single loop of the image the same size or larger than the viewport:

![原教程图示：Would increasing repeat_times fix this? — 2d_parallax_repeat_good_norect.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_repeat_good_norect.webp)

If you think of how the image scrolls across the screen, it starts by displaying what's inside the red rectangle
(determined by [repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size)), and when it reaches what's inside the yellow
rectangle it zips the image forward to give the illusion of scrolling forever.

![原教程图示：Would increasing repeat_times fix this? — 2d_parallax_repeat_good.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_repeat_good.webp)

If you have the image positioned away from the "infinite repeat canvas", when the camera reaches the yellow rectangle,
half of the image is cut off before it jumps forward like in the image below:

![原教程图示：Would increasing repeat_times fix this? — 2d_parallax_repeat_bad.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_repeat_bad.webp)

#### Scroll offset

If your parallax textures are already working correctly, but you prefer it to start at a different point,
[Parallax2D](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d) comes with a [scroll_offset](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-scroll-offset) property
used to offset where the infinite repeat canvas starts. As an example, if your image is 288x208, setting
the [scroll_offset](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-scroll-offset) to `(-144,0)` or `(144,0)` allows it to begin
halfway across the image.

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Repeat times
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
#### Repeat times

Ideally, following this guide, your parallax textures are large enough to cover the screen even when zoomed out.
Until now, we have had a perfectly fitting 288x208 texture inside of a 288x208 viewport. However, problems
occur when we zoom out by setting the [Camera2D.zoom](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_camera2d.html#class-camera2d-property-zoom) to `(0.5, 0.5)`:

![原教程图示：Repeat times — 2d_parallax_zoom_single.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_zoom_single.webp)

Even though everything is correctly set for the viewport at the default zoom level, zooming out makes it smaller than
the viewport, breaking the infinite repeat effect. This is where
[repeat_times](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-times) can help out. Setting a value of `3` (one extra
repeat behind and in front), it is now large enough to accommodate the infinite repeat effect.

![原教程图示：Repeat times — 2d_parallax_zoom_repeat_times.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_zoom_repeat_times.webp)

If these textures were meant to be repeated vertically, we would have specified a `y` value for the
[repeat_size](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-size). The
[repeat_times](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallax2d.html#class-parallax2d-property-repeat-times) would automatically add a repeat above and below as well.
This is only a horizontal parallax, so it leaves an empty block above and below the image. How do we solve this? We
need to get creative! In this example, we stretch the sky higher, and grass sprite lower. The textures now support the
normal zoom level and zooming out to half size.

![原教程图示：Repeat times — 2d_parallax_zoom_repeat_adjusted.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_zoom_repeat_adjusted.webp)

#### Split screen

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Split screen
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Most tutorials for making a split screen game in Godot begin by writing a small script to assign
the [Viewport.world_2d](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_viewport.html#class-viewport-property-world-2d) of the first SubViewport to the second, so they have a
shared display. Questions often pop up about how to share a parallax effect between both screens.

The parallax effect fakes a perspective by moving the positions of different textures in relation to the camera. This is
understandably problematic if you have multiple cameras, because your textures can't be in two places at once!

This is still achievable by cloning the parallax nodes into the second (or third or fourth)
[SubViewport](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_subviewport.html#class-subviewport). Here's how a setup looks for a two player game:

![原教程图示：Split screen — 2d_parallax_splitscreen.webp](../../assets/game-development/DEV-024/2d_parallax_splitscreen.webp)

Of course, now both backgrounds show in both SubViewports. What we want is for each parallax to only show in their
corresponding viewport. We can achieve this by doing the following:

- Leave all parallax nodes at their default [visibility_layer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-visibility-layer) of 1.
- Set the first SubViewport's [canvas_cull_mask](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_viewport.html#class-viewport-property-canvas-cull-mask) to only layers 1 and 2.
- Do the same for the second SubViewport but use layers 1 and 3.
- Give your parallax nodes in the first SubViewport a common parent and set its [visibility_layer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-visibility-layer) to 2.
- Do the same for the second SubViewport's parallax nodes, but use a layer of 3.

title: Parallax2D：循环背景与多层视差
heading: Split screen
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
How does this work? If a canvas item has a [visibility_layer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-visibility-layer) that
doesn't match the SubViewport's [canvas_cull_mask](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_viewport.html#class-viewport-property-canvas-cull-mask), it will hide all
children, even if they do. We use this to our advantage, letting the SubViewports cut off rendering of parallax nodes
whose parent doesn't have a supported [visibility_layer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvasitem.html#class-canvasitem-property-visibility-layer).

#### Previewing in the editor

Prior to 4.3, the recommendation was to place every layer in their own
[ParallaxBackground](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallaxbackground.html#class-parallaxbackground), enable the
[follow_viewport_enabled](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvaslayer.html#class-canvaslayer-property-follow-viewport-enabled) property, and scale the individual
layer. This method has always been tricky to get right, but is still achievable by using a
[CanvasLayer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_canvaslayer.html#class-canvaslayer) instead of a [ParallaxBackground](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_parallaxbackground.html#class-parallaxbackground).

Note

Another recommendation is [KoBeWi's "Parallax2D Preview" addon](https://github.com/KoBeWi/Godot-Parallax2D-Preview).
It provides a few different preview modes and is very handy!

author: Pedro Medeiros (Saint11)
text:
# 像素UI九宫格：固定角、可平铺边与文字区

让一个像素面板覆盖不同宽高，同时保留角部与边缘的像素结构。

## 原图与静态辅助图

![第一张原图展示九宫格、横竖扩展、标题/页脚变体和三段条形；第二张是同一教程的corner、edge、middle命名图，不另计新教程。](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice.gif)

![UI-9-Slice.gif 第0帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-frame-000.png)

![UI-9-Slice.gif 第24帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-frame-024.png)

![UI-9-Slice.gif 第48帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-frame-048.png)

![第一张原图展示九宫格、横竖扩展、标题/页脚变体和三段条形；第二张是同一教程的corner、edge、middle命名图，不另计新教程。](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-names.gif)

![UI-9-Slice-names.gif 第0帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-names-frame-000.png)

![UI-9-Slice-names.gif 第2帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-names-frame-002.png)

![UI-9-Slice-names.gif 第3帧截取（0开始，非逐帧全集）](../../assets/supplement/UI-001/UI-9-Slice-names-frame-003.png)

## 读图

第一张原图展示九宫格、横竖扩展、标题/页脚变体和三段条形；第二张是同一教程的corner、edge、middle命名图，不另计新教程。

## 根据原图整理的步骤

1. 把矩形拆成4个角、4条边和中心；角部保持尺寸，横边只沿横向扩展，竖边只沿纵向扩展。
2. 原图建议边缘能与角及自身重复衔接；中心与边缘少放高频细节，角部可以更丰富。
3. 边缘优先重复平铺。原作者提醒拉伸只适合很少细节的边；像素图仍要检查实际显示后的网格。
4. 给标题、页脚或特殊顶部另作变体，不必强迫所有面板共用一个外框。
5. 细长的血条、滑块和分隔条可以用三段切片；是否横向或竖向由伸展方向决定。

## 练习（整理者补充）

整理者练习：为背包做窄提示框、宽物品说明框和高列表框，复用同一组角与边；把真实长中文描述放入中部安静区域。

## 验收（整理者补充）

- [ ] 角部没有拉伸变形
- [ ] 相邻边重复无明显接缝
- [ ] 文字没有压到纹理与装饰
- [ ] 选中、按下、焦点和禁用仍可区分

## 适用边界

原图讲的是切片结构，不提供输入逻辑、可访问性认证或引擎按钮状态实现。 原图为教学材料；不可把阅读或插入参考图说成已制作游戏美术。

作者Pedro Medeiros（Saint11），[固定来源](https://github.com/saint11/Saint11Tutorials/blob/ce1393eb2c46441d917134a9fd52e15575ee10a7/UI-9-Slice.gif)。仓库[README许可声明](https://github.com/saint11/Saint11Tutorials/blob/ce1393eb2c46441d917134a9fd52e15575ee10a7/README.md)为[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)。原GIF保持原样；PNG为抽帧；中文为人工读图整理而非逐字OCR；练习与验收为整理者补充。新增内容继续按CC BY 4.0提供并保留原作者署名。

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

使用Theme资源统一项目界面的颜色、字体、图标与StyleBox，并理解局部覆盖的优先级。

## 前提

- DEV-001
- 基本Control节点

## 中文操作路线

1. 先列出按钮、标签和面板在项目中共享的颜色、字体大小、图标和背景外观。
2. 创建共享Theme资源，在项目级或Control分支根节点应用，并在各独立场景预览。
3. 使用type variation区分Header等语义角色，避免每个节点重复局部修改。
4. 焦点StyleBox覆盖在基础状态上；设计为边缘或适当透明的框，避免遮住普通/按下外观。
5. 出现不一致时先检查local override，再查最近的父Control主题和项目主题，避免误改全局资源。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

整理者练习：用同一Theme做背包、商店与设置三张面板，修改一个字体参数后检查三处都更新；刻意保留一个局部覆盖并解释其例外原因。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 组件状态语义一致
- [ ] 局部覆盖有明确理由
- [ ] 焦点可见且不掩盖按下状态
- [ ] 长中文文案可读

## 版本与边界

本篇是主题机制，原站游戏示例图不等于可直接复用的UI成品素材。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Introduction to GUI skinning

It is essential for a game to provide clear, informative, and yet visually
pleasing user interface to its players. While [Control](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_control.html#class-control)
nodes come with a decently functional look out of the box, there is always
room for uniqueness and case-specific tuning. For this purpose Godot engine
includes a system for GUI skinning (or theming), which allows you to customize
the look of every control in your user interface, including your custom controls.

Here is an example of this system in action — a game with the GUI that is
radically different from the default UI theme of the engine:

![原教程图示：Introduction to GUI skinning — tank-kings-by-winterpixel-games.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-002/tank-kings-by-winterpixel-games.png)


A "Gear Up!" screen in Tank Kings, courtesy of Winterpixel Games

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Introduction to GUI skinning
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Beyond achieving a unique look for your game, this system also enables developers
to provide customization options to the end users, including accessibility settings.
UI themes are applied in a cascading manner (i.e. they propagate from parent
controls to their children), which means that font settings or adjustments for
colorblind users can be applied in a single place and affect the entire UI tree.
Of course this system can also be used for gameplay purposes: your hero-based game
can change its style for the selected player character, or you can give different
flavors to the sides in your team-based project.

#### Basics of themes

The skinning system is driven by the [Theme](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_theme.html#class-theme) resource. Every
Godot project has an inherent default theme that contains the settings used by
the built-in control nodes. This is what gives the controls their distinct look
out of the box. A theme only describes the configuration, however, and it is still
the job of each individual control to use that configuration in the way it requires
to display itself. This is important to remember when implementing
[your own custom controls](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/ui/custom_gui_controls.html#doc-custom-gui-controls).

Note

Even the Godot editor itself relies on the default theme. But it doesn't look the
same as a Godot project, because it applies its own heavily customized theme on top
of the default one. In principle, this works exactly like it would in your game
as explained [below](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/ui/gui_skinning.html#doc-gui-theme-in-project).

##### Theme items

The configuration that is stored in a theme consists of theme items. Each item has
a unique name and must be one of the following data types:

- **Color**

  A [color](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_color.html#class-color) value, which is often used for fonts
  and backgrounds. Colors can also be used for modulation of controls
  and icons.
- **Constant**

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Theme items
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
An integer value, which can be used either for numeric properties of
  controls (such as the item separation in a [BoxContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_boxcontainer.html#class-boxcontainer)),
  or for boolean flags (such as the drawing of relationship lines in a [Tree](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_tree.html#class-tree)).
- **Font**

  A [font](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_font.html#class-font) resource, which is used by controls that
  display text. Fonts contain most text rendering settings, except for
  its size and color. On top of that, alignment and text direction are
  controlled by individual controls.
- **Font size**

  An integer value, which is used alongside a font to determine the
  size at which the text should be displayed.
- **Icon**

  A [texture](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_texture2d.html#class-texture2d) resource, which is normally used
  to display an icon (on a [Button](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_button.html#class-button), for example).
- **StyleBox**

  A [StyleBox](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_stylebox.html#class-stylebox) resource, a collection of configuration
  options which define the way a UI panel should be displayed. This is
  not limited to the [Panel](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_panel.html#class-panel) control, as styleboxes
  are used by many controls for their backgrounds and overlays.

  Different controls will apply StyleBoxes in a different manner. Most notably,
  `focus` styleboxes are drawn as an *overlay* to other styleboxes (such as
  `normal` or `pressed`) to allow the base stylebox to remain visible.
  This means the focus stylebox should be designed as an outline or translucent
  box, so that its background can remain visible.

##### Theme types

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Theme types
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
To help with the organization of its items each theme is separated into types,
and each item must belong to a single type. In other words, each theme item
is defined by its name, its data type and its theme type. This combination
must be unique within the theme. For example, there cannot be two color items named
`font_color` in a type called `Label`, but there can be another `font_color`
item in a type `LineEdit`.

The default Godot theme comes with multiple theme types already defined,
one for every built-in control node that uses UI skinning. The example above
contains actual theme items present in the default theme. You can refer to the
**Theme Properties** section in the class reference for each control to see
which items are available to it and its child classes.

Note

Child classes can use theme items defined for their parent class (`Button`
and its derivatives being a good example of that). In fact, every control can
use every theme item of any theme type, if it needs to (but for the clarity and
predictability we try to avoid that in the engine).

It is important to remember that for child classes that process is automated.
Whenever a built-in control requests a theme item from the theme it can omit
the theme type, and its class name will be used instead. On top of that,
the class names of its parent classes will also be used in turn. This allows
changes to the parent class, such as `Button`, to affect all derived
classes without the need to customize every one of them.

You can also define your own theme types, and additionally customize both built-in
controls and your own controls. Because built-in controls have no knowledge of
your custom theme types, you must utilize scripts to access those items. All control
nodes have several methods that allow you to fetch theme items from the theme that
is applied to them. Those methods accept the theme type as one of the arguments.

```gdscript
var accent_color = get_theme_color("accent_color", "MyType")
label.add_theme_color_override("font_color", accent_color)
```

```csharp
Color accentColor = GetThemeColor("accent_color", "MyType");
label.AddThemeColorOverride("font_color", accentColor);
```

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Theme types
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
To give more customization opportunities types can also be linked together as
type variations. This is another use-case for custom theme types. For example,
a theme can contain a type `Header` which can be marked as a variation of
the base `Label` type. An individual `Label` control can then be set to
use the `Header` variation for its type, and every time a theme item is
requested from a theme this variation will be used before any other type. This
allows to store various presets of theme items for the same class of the
control node in the single `Theme` resource.

Warning

Only variations available from the default theme or defined in the custom
project theme are shown in the Inspector dock as options. You can still
input manually the name of a variation that is defined outside of those
two places, but it is recommended to keep all variations to the project theme.

You can learn more about creating and using theme type variations in a
[dedicated article](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/ui/gui_theme_type_variations.html#doc-gui-theme-type-variations).

#### Customizing a control

Each control node can be customized directly without the use of themes. This
is called local overrides. Every theme property from the control's class
reference can be overridden directly on the control itself, using either
the Inspector dock, or scripts. This allows to make granular changes to a
particular part of the UI, while not affecting anything else in the project,
including this control's children.

![原教程图示：Customizing a control — themecheck.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-002/themecheck.webp)

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Customizing a control
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Local overrides are less useful for the visual flair of your user interface,
especially if you aim for consistency. However, for layout nodes these are
essential. Nodes such as [BoxContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_boxcontainer.html#class-boxcontainer) and
[GridContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_gridcontainer.html#class-gridcontainer) use theme constants for defining
separation between their children, and [MarginContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_margincontainer.html#class-margincontainer)
stores its customizable margins in its theme items.

Whenever a control has a local theme item override, this is the value that
it uses. Values provided by the theme are ignored.

#### Customizing a project

Out of the box each project adopts the default project theme provided by Godot. The
default theme itself is constant and cannot be changed, but its items can be overridden
with a custom theme. Custom themes can be applied in two ways: as a project setting,
and as a node property throughout the tree of control nodes.

There are two project settings that can be adjusted to affect your entire project:
[GUI > Theme > Custom](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-gui-theme-custom) allows you to
set a custom project-wide theme, and [GUI > Theme > Custom Font](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_projectsettings.html#class-projectsettings-property-gui-theme-custom-font)
does the same to the default fallback font. When a theme item is requested by a control
node the custom project theme, if present, is checked first. Only if it doesn't have
the item the default theme is checked.

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Customizing a project
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
This allows you to configure the default look of every Godot control with a single
theme resource, but you can go more granular than that. Every control node also has
a [theme](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_control.html#class-control-property-theme) property, which allows you to set a
custom theme for the branch of nodes starting with that control. This means that the
control and all of its children, and their children in turn, would first check that
custom theme resource before falling back on the project and the default themes.

Note

Instead of changing the project setting you can set the custom theme resource to the
root-most control node of your entire UI branch to almost the same effect. While in the
running project it will behave as expected, individual scenes will still display
using the default theme when previewing or running them directly. To fix that you
can set the same theme resource to the root control of each individual scene.

For example, you can have a certain style for buttons in your project theme, but want
a different look for buttons inside of a popup dialog. You can set a custom theme
resource to the root control of your popup and define a different style for buttons
within that resource. As long as the chain of control nodes between the root of
the popup and the buttons is uninterrupted, those buttons will use the styles defined
in the theme resource that is closest to them. All other controls will still be styled
using the project-wide theme and the default theme styles.

To sum it up, for an arbitrary control its theme item lookup would look something
like this:

1. Check for local overrides of the same data type and name.
2. Using control's type variation, class name and parent class names:

title: 游戏UI主题：颜色、字体、图标与状态外观的统一
heading: Customizing a project
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
1. Check every control starting from itself and see if it has a theme property set;
   2. If it does, check that theme for the matching item of the same name, data and theme type;
   3. If there is no custom theme or it doesn't have the item, move to the parent control;
   4. Repeat steps a-c. until the root of the tree is reached, or a non-control node is reached.
3. Using control's type variation, class name and parent class names check the project-wide theme, if it's present.
4. Using control's type variation, class name and parent class names check the default theme.

Even if the item doesn't exist in any theme, a corresponding default value for that
data type will be returned.

#### Beyond controls

Naturally, themes are an ideal type of resource for storing configuration for
something visual. While the support for theming is built into control nodes,
other nodes can use them as well, just like any other resource.

An example of using themes for something beyond controls can be a modulation
of sprites for the same units on different teams in a strategy game. A theme
resource can define a collection of colors, and sprites (with a help from scripts)
can use those colors to draw the texture. The main benefit being that you
could make different themes using the same theme items for red, blue, and
green teams, and swap them with a single resource change.

author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 游戏UI布局：容器、物品网格、长文本与可变尺寸

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

用布局容器组织背包网格、属性行与可滚动说明，避免图文重叠。

## 前提

- UI-002

## 中文操作路线

1. 选择适合信息结构的HBox/VBox/Grid或Margin等容器，不先把每个子控件固定到绝对位置。
2. 加入Container的Control子节点由父容器管理位置；手工拖动结果可能在下一次布局时被覆盖。
3. 分别检查横向和纵向的Fill、Expand和Shrink设置，控制谁获得剩余空间。
4. 用嵌套容器组合物品网格、说明区和底部操作；用PanelContainer保留面板样式边距。
5. 加入最长名称、最大数量和最低支持窗口尺寸；必要时滚动或重排，避免把全部文本缩得更小。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

整理者练习：做一个4列背包和物品说明面板；使用短名、长中文名、99与9999数量以及空物品栏测试。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 容器调整时不覆盖文字
- [ ] 按钮仍在可视区域
- [ ] 扩展与收缩行为能解释
- [ ] 九宫格装饰不占正文空间

## 版本与边界

容器决定布局，不决定美术风格。原文提及某些工具式UI，不要求把游戏改成网页仪表盘。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Using Containers

[Anchors](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/tutorials/ui/size_and_anchors.html#doc-size-and-anchors) are an efficient way to handle
different aspect ratios for basic multiple resolution handling in GUIs.

For more complex user interfaces, they can become difficult to use.

This is often the case of games, such as RPGs, online chats, tycoons or simulations. Another
common case where more advanced layout features may be required is in-game tools (or simply just tools).

All these situations require a more capable OS-like user interface, with advanced layout and formatting.
For that, [Containers](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_container.html#class-container) are more useful.

#### Container layout

Containers provide a huge amount of layout power (as an example, the Godot editor user interface is entirely done using them):

> ![原教程图示：Container layout — godot_containers.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/godot_containers.png)

title: 游戏UI布局：容器、物品网格、长文本与可变尺寸
heading: Container layout
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
When a [Container](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_container.html#class-container)-derived node is used, all children [Control](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_control.html#class-control) nodes give up their
own positioning ability. This means the *Container* will control their positioning and any attempt to manually alter these
nodes will be either ignored or invalidated the next time their parent is resized.

Likewise, when a *Container* derived node is resized, all its children will be re-positioned according to it,
with a behavior based on the type of container used:

> ![原教程图示：Container layout — container_example.gif](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/container_example.gif)

Example of *HBoxContainer* resizing children buttons.

The real strength of containers is that they can be nested (as nodes), allowing the creation of very complex layouts that resize effortlessly.

#### Sizing options

When adding a node to a container, the way the container treats each child depends mainly on their *container sizing options*. These options
can be found by inspecting the layout of any *Control* that is a child of a *Container*.

> ![原教程图示：Sizing options — container_sizing_options.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/container_sizing_options.webp)

Sizing options are independent for vertical and horizontal sizing and not all containers make use of them (but most do):

title: 游戏UI布局：容器、物品网格、长文本与可变尺寸
heading: Sizing options
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
- **Fill**: Ensures the control *fills* the designated area within the container. No matter if
  a control *expands* or not (see below), it will only *fill* the designated area when this is toggled on (it is by default).
- **Expand**: Attempts to use as much space as possible in the parent container (in each axis).
  Controls that don't expand will be pushed away by those that do. Between expanding controls, the
  amount of space they take from each other is determined by the *Stretch Ratio* (see below).
  This option is only available when the parent Container is of the right type, for example the *HBoxContainer* has this option
  for horizontal sizing.
- **Shrink Begin** When expanding, try to remain at the left or top of the expanded
  area.
- **Shrink Center** When expanding, try to remain at the center of the expanded
  area.
- **Shrink End** When expanding, try to remain at the right or bottom of the expanded
  area.
- **Stretch Ratio**: The ratio of how much expanded controls take up the available space in relation to each
  other. A control with "2", will take up twice as much available space as one with "1".

Experimenting with these flags and different containers is recommended to get a better grasp on how they work.

#### Container types

Godot provides several container types out of the box as they serve different purposes:

##### Box Containers

Arranges child controls vertically or horizontally (via [HBoxContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_hboxcontainer.html#class-hboxcontainer) and
[VBoxContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_vboxcontainer.html#class-vboxcontainer)). In the opposite of the designated direction
(as in, vertical for a horizontal container), it just expands the children.

> ![原教程图示：Box Containers — containers_box.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_box.png)

These containers make use of the *Stretch Ratio* property for children with the *Expand* flag set.

##### Grid Container

title: 游戏UI布局：容器、物品网格、长文本与可变尺寸
heading: Grid Container
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Arranges child controls in a grid layout (via [GridContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_gridcontainer.html#class-gridcontainer), amount
of columns must be specified). Uses both the vertical and horizontal expand flags.

> ![原教程图示：Grid Container — containers_grid.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_grid.png)

##### Margin Container

Child controls are expanded towards the bounds of this control (via
[MarginContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_margincontainer.html#class-margincontainer)). Padding will be added on the margins
depending on the theme configuration.

> ![原教程图示：Margin Container — containers_margin.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_margin.png)

Again, keep in mind that the margins are a *Theme* value, so they need to be edited from the
constants overrides section of each control:

> ![原教程图示：Margin Container — containers_margin_constants.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_margin_constants.png)

##### Tab Container

Allows you to place several child controls stacked on top of each other (via
[TabContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_tabcontainer.html#class-tabcontainer)), with only the *current* one visible.

> ![原教程图示：Tab Container — containers_tab.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_tab.png)

Changing the *current* one is done via tabs located at the top of the container, via clicking:

> ![原教程图示：Tab Container — containers_tab_click.gif](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_tab_click.gif)

The titles are generated from the node names by default (although they can be overridden via *TabContainer* API).

Settings such as tab placement and *StyleBox* can be modified in the *TabContainer* theme overrides.

##### Split Container

title: 游戏UI布局：容器、物品网格、长文本与可变尺寸
heading: Split Container
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
Accepts only one or two children controls, then places them side to side with a divisor
(via [HSplitContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_hsplitcontainer.html#class-hsplitcontainer) and [VSplitContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_vsplitcontainer.html#class-vsplitcontainer)).
Respects both horizontal and vertical flags, as well as *Ratio*.

> ![原教程图示：Split Container — containers_split.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_split.png)

The divisor can be dragged around to change the size relation between both children:

> ![原教程图示：Split Container — containers_split_drag.gif](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_split_drag.gif)

##### PanelContainer

A container that draws a *StyleBox*, then expands children to cover its whole area
(via [PanelContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_panelcontainer.html#class-panelcontainer), respecting the *StyleBox* margins).
It respects both the horizontal and vertical sizing options.

> ![原教程图示：PanelContainer — containers_panel.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_panel.png)

This container is useful as a top-level control, or just to add custom backgrounds to sections of a layout.

##### FoldableContainer

A container that can be expanded/collapsed
(via [FoldableContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_foldablecontainer.html#class-foldablecontainer)).
Child controls are hidden when it is collapsed.

##### ScrollContainer

Accepts a single child node. If the child node is bigger than the container, scrollbars will be added
to allow panning the node around (via [ScrollContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_scrollcontainer.html#class-scrollcontainer)). Both
vertical and horizontal size options are respected, and the behavior can be turned on or off
per axis in the properties.

> ![原教程图示：ScrollContainer — containers_scroll.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_scroll.png)

Mouse wheel and touch drag (when touch is available) are also valid ways to pan the child control around.

title: 游戏UI布局：容器、物品网格、长文本与可变尺寸
heading: ScrollContainer
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
> ![原教程图示：ScrollContainer — containers_center_pan.gif](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_center_pan.gif)

As in the example above, one of the most common ways to use this container is together with a *VBoxContainer* as child.

##### AspectRatioContainer

A container type that arranges its child controls in a way that preserves their proportions
automatically when the container is resized.
(via [AspectRatioContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_aspectratiocontainer.html#class-aspectratiocontainer)).
It has multiple stretch modes, providing options for adjusting the child controls' sizes concerning the container:
"fill," "width control height," "height control width," and "cover."

> ![原教程图示：AspectRatioContainer — containers_aspectratio.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_aspectratio.webp)

It is useful when you have a container that needs to be dynamic and responsive to different screen sizes,
and you want the child elements to scale proportionally without losing their intended shapes.

> ![原教程图示：AspectRatioContainer — containers_aspectratio_drag.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_aspectratio_drag.webp)

##### FlowContainer

FlowContainer is a container that arranges its child controls either horizontally or vertically
(via [HFlowContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_hflowcontainer.html#class-hflowcontainer) and via [VFlowContainer](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.5/classes/class_vflowcontainer.html#class-vflowcontainer)).
When the available space runs out, it wraps the children to the next line or column, similar to how text wraps in a book.

> ![原教程图示：FlowContainer — containers_hflow.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_hflow.webp)

It is useful for creating flexible layouts where the child controls adjust automatically to the available space without overlapping.

> ![原教程图示：FlowContainer — containers_hflow_drag.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-003/containers_hflow_drag.webp)

##### CenterContainer

title: 游戏HUD锚点：宽高比变化中的定位与安全边距
heading: 游戏HUD锚点：宽高比变化中的定位与安全边距
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
# 游戏HUD锚点：宽高比变化中的定位与安全边距

> 本文由 Godot 官方 4.5 版文档转换。下方中文导读、练习和验收是整理者的教学编排，英文正文是原教程主内容；不是官方中文逐句译文，也未声称已在引擎中执行全部练习。

## 适用任务

让角落HUD、居中弹窗和边缘控件在窗口变化时维持合理关系。

## 前提

- DEV-020

## 中文操作路线

1. 确认Control以父Control或视口作为参考。
2. 用0到1的anchor位置表示相对边缘，用offset描述相对于anchor的像素距离。
3. 固定在右下角的控件按右/下锚点设置偏移；居中控件可采用0.5锚点与半尺寸的正负偏移。
4. 使用编辑器Anchor预设提高效率，再检查是否需要容器接管复杂排布。
5. 在多个宽高比和界面倍率下检查四角HUD、居中面板、文字与安全边距。

## 图示怎么读

先沿英文正文的步骤阅读对应截图；截图来自同一版本页面，局部操作顺序以紧邻图片的文字为准。图片下载到本地，可离线打开并放大检查。截图中的示例美术用于说明引擎操作，不代表本库要求采用该画风。

## 动手练习

整理者练习：为像素村庄做左上状态、右下快捷栏和居中对话框，改变窗口宽高比并记录它们各自的参考边。

## 验收清单

- [ ] 关键HUD未出屏
- [ ] 弹窗居中且文字未截断
- [ ] offset与anchor的意义清楚
- [ ] 游戏世界像素倍率与UI阅读倍率分别考虑

## 版本与边界

锚点是布局关系，不是整数像素缩放的替代方案；清晰度还需DEV-021与DEV-022。

本次来源固定为 Godot 4.5 文档分支，抓取日期为 2026-10-29；它不是“当前最新版本”的声明。升级引擎时应重新核对节点名、属性名和 API。

## 原教程正文（英文，Markdown 转换）

### Size and anchors

If a game was always going to be run on the same device and at the same
resolution, positioning controls would be a simple matter of setting the
position and size of each one of them. Unfortunately, that is rarely the
case.

While some configurations may be more common than others, devices like
phones, tablets and portable gaming consoles can vary greatly. Therefore,
we often have to account for different aspect ratios, resolutions and user
scaling.

There are several ways to account for this, but for now, let's just imagine
that the screen resolution has changed and the controls need to be
re-positioned. Some will need to follow the bottom of the screen, others
the top of the screen, or maybe the right or left margins.

![原教程图示：Size and anchors — anchors.png](../../assets/game-development/UI-004/anchors.png)

This is done by editing the *anchor offsets* of controls, which behave similar
to a margin. To access these settings, you will first need to select the *Custom*
anchor preset.

Each control has four anchor offsets: left, right, bottom, and top, which correspond
to the respective edges of the control. By default, all of
them represent a distance in pixels relative to the top-left corner of
the parent control or (in case there is no parent control) the viewport.

title: 游戏HUD锚点：宽高比变化中的定位与安全边距
heading: Size and anchors
author: Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur and the Godot community
text:
![原教程图示：Size and anchors — offset.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-004/offset.webp)

So to make the control wider you can make the right offset larger and/or
make the left offset smaller. This lets you set the exact placement
and shape of the control.

The *anchor* properties adjust where the offsets are relative *to*.
Each offset has an individual anchor that can be adjusted from the
beginning to the end of the parent. So the vertical (top, bottom) anchors
adjust from `0.0` (top of parent) to `1.0` (bottom of parent) with `0.5` being
the center, and the control offsets will be placed relative to that
point. The horizontal (left, right) anchors similarly adjust from left to
right of the parent.

Note that when you wish the edge of a control to be above or left of the
anchor point, you must change the offset value to be negative.

For example: when horizontal anchors are changed to `1.0`, the offset values
become relative to the top-right corner of the parent control or viewport.

![原教程图示：Size and anchors — offset_end.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-004/offset_end.webp)

Adjusting the two horizontal or the two vertical anchors to different
values will make the control change size when the parent control does.
Here, the control is set to anchor its bottom-right corner to the
parent's bottom-right, while the top-left control offsets are still
anchored to the top-left of the parent, so when re-sizing the parent,
the control will always cover it, leaving a 20 pixel offset:

![原教程图示：Size and anchors — offset_around.webp](../../assets/game-development/UI-004/offset_around.webp)
